💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Calum Burrowes | 26 Nov 2026 12:11, Last updated: 26 Nov 2026 12:20.
  • Meeting for the first time in their history, League One newcomers Bromley will be looking to climb out of the relegation zone when they welcome Burton Albion to Hayes Lane on Saturday afternoon.
  • The Ravens will be aiming to make it three league matches unbeaten after following up a win over Reading with a home draw against Wycombe Wanderers on Tuesday night, while the Brewers will be hoping to end their three-game losing streak after suffering a 2-1 defeat to an in-form Luton Town side last Saturday.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Calum Burrowes | 26 Nov 2026 12:11, Last updated: 26 Nov 2026 12:20.

Meeting for the first time in their history, League One newcomers Bromley will be looking to climb out of the relegation zone when they welcome Burton Albion to Hayes Lane on Saturday afternoon.

The Ravens will be aiming to make it three league matches unbeaten after following up a win over Reading with a home draw against Wycombe Wanderers on Tuesday night, while the Brewers will be hoping to end their three-game losing streak after suffering a 2-1 defeat to an in-form Luton Town side last Saturday.

After securing promotion to the third tier for the first time in their history last May under the stewardship of long-serving manager Andy Woodman, Bromley were expected to face a difficult first season at this level, with the club having every reason to stick by the man who had guided them to two promotions in three seasons and taken them from the National League to League One.

However, Woodman's five-and-a-half-year spell at the club came to an abrupt end in late October after a 4-0 defeat to Leicester City left the Ravens 23rd in the table following 10 matches, a decision that came as a surprise and disappointment to many Bromley supporters.

The London-based side turned to former MK Dons, Charlton Athletic, Oxford United and Salford City boss Karl Robinson, who will take charge of his fifth match as Bromley manager this weekend.

Robinson's arrival was followed by exits from both the FA Cup and EFL Trophy in his opening two matches, but he has since managed to steady the ship in the league, guiding his side to a narrow victory over Reading before they followed that up with a draw at home to Wycombe Wanderers during the week, leaving him unbeaten in League One since taking charge.

Those four points from their last two outings have provided some much-needed momentum ahead of a busy festive period, although Bromley remain in the bottom four with 13 points to their name, meaning a fourth league victory of the season could be enough to lift the Ravens out of the relegation zone ahead of the final month of the calendar year.

As for Burton Albion, they make the journey to Greater London from Staffordshire hoping to bring an end to a three-match losing streak in League One that has seen them slip out of the top half and move dangerously close to the relegation places.

A victory in their final home fixture of October against Leyton Orient was followed by defeats to Wycombe Wanderers, MK Dons and, most recently, Luton Town, with the second of those losses proving particularly damaging as they were beaten 6-2 at Stadium MK.

The Halloween defeat to the Chairboys was at least followed by a 4-0 FA Cup victory over AFC Rushden and Diamonds at the start of November, but that remains Burton's only win in their last five matches across all competitions, a run that has also included a defeat to Notts County in the EFL Trophy.

Although their heavy loss to MK Dons came against an in-form side, Burton's own defensive record has taken a significant hit, with Gary Bowyer's men now having conceded 29 goals in their 16 League One outings, a tally bettered only by their upcoming opponents.

With that noted, only two teams in the bottom half of the table have scored more than the Brewers, highlighting that Bowyer's side have an attacking foundation to build on if they can turn their fortunes around sooner rather than later.

A victory in their first-ever meeting with Bromley could lift Burton as high as 15th and give them a seven-point cushion over the League One relegation zone.

Bromley form (all competitions):.

Burton Albion form (all competitions):.

Having collected four points from his opening two league matches in charge of Bromley, Robinson will be keen to maintain some consistency ahead of the weekend fixture, and he has the option of keeping the same side after coming through Tuesday's draw without any further injury concerns.

Defender Kamarl Grant scored their only goal last time out and could partner makeshift centre-back George Saville once again, unless former West Ham United and Augsburg defender Reece Oxford is ready to make his second appearance of the season after featuring against Reading in what was his first competitive outing in more than four years.

Robinson's relationship with Ravens winger Jodi Jones is reportedly strained following events during their time at previous clubs, and the former Notts County attacker is expected to remain on the bench for this encounter.

As for Burton, they are likely to be forced into a change after Joe Lewis was forced off with an injury late in their defeat to Luton, with the defender expected to miss out and potentially be replaced by Jason Sraha.

Lewis is set to join several teammates in the treatment room, with Finn Delap, George Evans, Kyran Lofthouse and Caylan Vickers also expected to remain sidelined due to various injury and fitness concerns, leaving the Brewers unable to fill their matchday squad in recent weeks.

Matthew Dennis, however, returned to the team after missing just one fixture and could come back into the starting lineup to lead the line, potentially at the expense of either Mark O'Mahony or Gbemi Arubi.

Emeka Adeile has started just two league matches all season but has scored in consecutive appearances and is expected to retain his place out wide on Saturday afternoon.

Bromley possible starting lineup:.

George; Ifill, Grant, Oxford, Mendy; Pinnock, McKiernan, Conteh, Archer; Whitely, Adeboyejo.

Burton Albion possible starting lineup:.

Addai; Sibbick, Sraha, Tilt; Rodrigues, Chauke, Krubally, Adeile; Collar; O'Mahony, Dennis.

With both sides heading into December embroiled in an unwanted battle near the bottom of the table, they will be eager to pick up valuable points, move further clear of danger and build some much-needed momentum.

We expect the pair to play out a 1-1 draw, allowing Robinson to maintain his unbeaten start to life as Bromley manager in League One.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Tomorrow evening, AC Milan will entrust Ardon Jashari with the job of filling Luka Modric’s shoes, after the Croatian’s injury.

If you missed last night’s reporting, Milan have been dealt a bit of a blow ahead of their game against Olympiacos, as Modric has suffered a muscle strain. It’s not a major one, and he should be back for next weekend’s game.

Sources indicate that nevertheless, it creates a short-term concern and in a midfield where only a few names have convinced, it plunges Ruben Amorim into the water somewhat. There is a solution, though, and it would be ideal if he stepped up.

According to recent reports, since he arrived, Jashari has been seen as the next in line for Modric, but he’s never shown performances to match that eventual rise. However, Gazzetta dello Sport (as seen below) write that he could take that step against Olympiacos.

In a recent development, it’s a potential turning point for the Swiss, who still has the faith of the club and the fans, especially after his first goal at the weekend. So, with it being a necessity that he comes into the team here, a solid performance is needed.

It opens a space for Jashari, but filling Modric’s boots will not be an easy task. In fact, he’ll have to be at his best to replace him, especially in a game with so much on the line.

It has been revealed that looking at the Europa League table, the Rossoneri need to be perfect if they’re to have any chance of a top eight finish. For him, though, Jashari must be perfect if his journey at San Siro is to continue.

Industry observers note that so far, his time in Italy has been marred by injury and a failure to establish himself as a starter, or even a key rotational option. Yet, the Diavolo never gave up on him, refusing a sale in the summer.

Now, it is time to repay that in a game where ‘everything looks different’. For Jashari, it’s a simple task: be solid. He’s got a guaranteed place, reliable teammates around him and the trust to act.

In a recent development, no one can challenge him for the next five days; the spot is guaranteed. It’ll be up to him if those five days become 10 or more. If not, there’s a market waiting for him.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Darren Plant | 26 Nov 2026 12:15.

Wolverhampton Wanderers make the trip to Lincoln City on Saturday afternoon looking to strengthen their hold of a top-three position in the Championship table.

Meanwhile, Lincoln play host to one of the form teams in the division having just sacked co-managers Chris Cohen and Tom Shaw.

Positives can be taken from Lincoln - last season's League One champions - reaching this stage of the season sitting three points above the relegation zone.

Nevertheless, Tuesday's 4-0 defeat at Charlton Athletic represented their fifth successive defeat and was the final straw for Lincoln's hierarchy.

Despite Cohen and Shaw arguably performing better than anticipated in their surprise role, Lincoln had also only recorded four points from their last 10 games, losing on eight occasions.

A change in direction has, theoretically, been made at the right time, and a permanent successor is expected to be selected ahead of the trip to Cardiff City on December 5.

For now, first-team coach Shaun Pearson and fellow backroom staff members will attempt to guide Lincoln to just their second home win in nine matches, their only such success having come against struggling Burnley by a 4-1 scoreline last month.

As for Wolves, they make the trip to the ProAmpac Stadium having recorded a 3-0 win over Derby County and having had the most shots (39) in a Championship fixture in 11 years.

For all the criticism that has come Cesar Peixoto's way, Wolves remain in third spot with 31 goals and 34 points from their 17 games.

An eight-match unbeaten streak has been put together, the West Midlands outfit picking up six wins and two draws since October 16.

Lincoln may take belief from Wolves only prevailing from four of their eight away games. That remarked, Peixoto's side have already made trips to the likes of West Ham United, Birmingham City, Sheffield United, Middlesbrough and Wrexham this season, suggesting that it is a far better record than in black and white.

Sonny Bradley, Yunus Konak, Dom Jeffries and Freddie Draper are all in contention for recalls to the team.

However, midfielder Conor McGrandles is again expected to miss out through injury.

Meanwhile, Peixoto could make a number of alterations, with Toti Gomes and Marshall Munetsi among those who could feature for Wolves.

Rodrigo Gomes may also get the nod over Rafiki Mentioned in the final third, while Adam Armstrong scoring on five of his last six appearances will see him keep his place ahead of Sean Neave.

Wickens; Coubis, Bradley, Elerewe, Towler; Reach, Konak, Varfolomeev, House; Street; Draper.

Sa; Trippier, Djiga, Krejci, T Gomes; Andre, Munetsi; R Gomes, Lopez, Mane; Armstrong.

By Matthew Cooper | 26 Nov 2026 12:22, Last updated: 26 Nov 2026 20:12.

Peterborough United will be looking to pick up an important victory when they welcome rivals Cambridge United to the Weston Homes Stadium on Saturday.

The hosts right now sit 22nd in the League One table, while the visitors are 11th.

Peterborough head into this local derby after ending a four-match winless run last weekend when they beat promotion chasers Plymouth Argyle 2-0.

Harry Ashfield opened the scoring in the first half, before Harry Leonard converted a penalty in stoppage-time to secure all three points.

The win was a welcome boost for Robbie Savage's side, who are fighting for survival and remain in the relegation zone with 13 points from 14 games.

However, they will be looking to carry the momentum of last weekend's win into Saturday's clash, with the Posh targeting back-to-back league victories for the first time since February.

It is also worth noting that Peterborough have a strong recent record against their rivals, having won their last five meetings across all competitions.

Cambridge, meanwhile, are without a win in their last five league games and suffered a disappointing 3-0 home defeat to league leaders Stockport County last Saturday.

Ollie Norwood broke the deadlock early in the second half with a stunning free kick, before Ethan Ennis doubled their lead and Gassan Ahadme scored an unfortunate own goal.

The defeat leaves the U's 11th with 21 points from 15 matches, having suffered just one defeat in their first 10 games before going five without a win.

Head coach Neil Harris has admitted his side have not been "tough to play against" in recent weeks and is keen for them to "get back to being that team".

Peterborough could welcome back Ben Woods and Luca Mendonca on Saturday, but they are both unlikely to start even if they are fit.

Savage is expected to keep faith with the team that beat Plymouth last weekend, with Leonard set to lead the line with support out wide from Bolu Shofowoke and Owura Edwards.

Cambridge may be forced to make at least one change, with the availability of Kelland Watts in doubt after he was forced off against Stockport.

Patrick Bauer could replace Watts in defence, while Louis Appere is set to start up front with support from Zak Bradshaw and Ben Knight.

Peterborough United possible starting lineup:.

Bass; Johnston, Feeney, Hughes, Mills; Jones, Ashfield; Shofowoke, Williams, Edwards; Leonard.

Cambridge United possible starting lineup:.

Peterborough should have renewed confidence after their victory over Plymouth and we are expecting a tight, hard-fought derby clash.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • European shares fell sharply in early trading on Friday as a global sell-off fueled by concerns over artificial intelligence stocks spread from Wall Street to Asia and Europe.
  • Fears of curbs on AI data-center spending have added to investors' concerns after Democrats won control of both chambers of the US Congress.
  • The pan-European STOXX 600 index dropped 1.6% in early trading, wiping out its gains for the week.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

European shares fell sharply in early trading on Friday as a global sell-off fueled by concerns over artificial intelligence stocks spread from Wall Street to Asia and Europe.

Fears of curbs on AI data-center spending have added to investors' concerns after Democrats won control of both chambers of the US Congress.

The pan-European STOXX 600 index dropped 1.6% in early trading, wiping out its gains for the week. Most major European markets fell more than 1%, with media, healthcare and retail stocks leading the declines.

European markets had previously weathered the week's turbulence better than their Asian and US counterparts because of their more limited exposure to AI stocks.

Earlier, Japanese and South Korean shares tumbled after a massive selloff in tech stocks on Wall Street the previous day.

Tokyo's benchmark Nikkei 225 index fell 5.5% in early trade, while Seoul's tech-heavy Kospi index slid as much as 8.8%, triggering a circuit breaker which suspended trading for 20 minutes. Taiwan's benchmark TAIEX index was also down more than 8%.

Asian tech giants including Samsung Electronics, SK Hynix and Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC) have borne the brunt of the artificial intelligence-related selloff.

Samsung plunged nearly 10% while SK Hynix slid over 11%.

Chip-related shares in Japan also took a beating, with Tokyo Electron stock trading down around 9% and Kioxia shedding 13%.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

US markets were hammered on Thursday by a sharp retreat in tech stocks, particularly those involved in the buildout of artificial intelligence infrastructure like data centers.

The tech-heavy Nasdaq fell 5.52% and shed as much as $2.5 trillion (roughly €2.23 trillion) in market value, while the broader S&P 500 index plunged 4.4%.

The rout occurred as investors grow increasingly anxious about the colossal AI spending intends and whether they will eventually produce commensurate profits.

The results of the US midterm elections, which saw Democrats seize control of both houses of US Congress, added to the concerns.

A number of Democratic governors-elect campaigned on slowing artificial intelligence development and promised to stop or pause the construction of data centers amid growing public opposition to such projects.

"It's pretty clear there's been a real shift ​in sentiment," Michael McCarthy, chief executive for Australia and Fresh Zealand at online brokerage Moomoo, told the Reuters news agency.

According to recent reports, "Market turning points are often accompanied by strong disagreement, and that shows up in the market ​by huge swings in either direction," he stated. "That's what we appear to have had — and last night's emphatic sell-down suggests that is the direction that we're now headed in.".

Rasmus Hojlund has laid bare the suffocating pressure of playing for Manchester United and given his insight into what Mauricio Pochettino’s squad will be suffering while marooned in the Premier League relegation zone.

The Dane was back in town this week after spending two seasons at United, mocking Manchester City fans when scoring the opener of Napoli’s 2-2 draw at the Etihad Stadium on Tuesday night.

Hojlund secured a £38million permanent move away from Old Trafford in the summer but remains in touch with plenty of old team-mates and believes the lack of equilibrium at the club has contributed to a steady decline.

‘There are so many people following the club around the world and you can’t really escape from it,’ Hojlund said.

‘It is almost too high when it is good and almost too low when it is bad. It is all about trying to be in that middle. I had both the highs and the lows there.

‘The pressure is part of the club, it comes with playing for United. There has been a lot of change but hopefully they will get it right with Mauricio.’.

Rasmus Hojlund mocked Man City fans after scoring for Napoli at the Etihad on Tuesday night.

According to recent reports, A United supporter, Hojlund laughed off the idea that the club is in a relegation scrap despite their worst start to a season since 1972. And the 23-year-old revealed that the players were ready for ‘change’ following the sacking of Michael Carrick.

‘I spoke with Bruno [Fernandes] and Diogo [Dalot] during the international break and they were all obviously devastated that Michael was going but also looking forward to some change,’ Hojlund added.

‘I am still speaking with Patrick [Dorgu] and I just wish the guys all the best. I am sure they will turn it around this season. They have got a lot of quality. They have got a great squad, good leaders, good professionals.

It has been revealed that ‘It is a temporary picture, I think they will get back to the top. The Premier League is like this. I read the other day that Bournemouth was in the relegation zone after a couple of games, now they have won the last five games and are in the top half of the table.’.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Carter White | 26 Nov 2026 12:22, Last updated: 26 Nov 2026 20:18.

Both aiming to halt their respective rotten runs of second-tier form, Millwall and Burnley lock horns at The Den in search of much-needed Championship points on Saturday afternoon.

The Lions were sentenced to another loss by promotion-chasing Stoke City earlier in the week, whilst the Clarets claimed an unwanted record in their 2-0 home defeat by Birmingham City.

After suffering just four Championship away defeats last season on their way to a third-placed finish, Millwall picked up their sixth loss on the road in 2026-27 at Stoke on Wednesday night.

The Lions extended their losing run to four consecutive matches following a lacklustre first-half display at the bet365 Stadium, where in-form striker George Hirst bagged a game-clinching brace for the hosts.

Winning just one of their past eight second-tier matches (D1 L6), Alex Neil's side have plummeted down to 18th spot in the Championship standings, a mammoth nine points behind the current top-eight pace.

Following four straight losses on the road, Millwall are in desperate need of some home comforts this weekend; however, the Lions have enjoyed victory in just one of their past six (D2 L3) competitive contests at The Den.

One of a multitude of problems facing head coach Neil ahead of a hectic festive period, the South Londoners are struggling in attack since the summer departure of Femi Azeez, scoring only once across their past four matches.

Whilst Millwall are experiencing a saddening fall from grace relative to last season, Saturday's visitors Burnley are in the midst of a full-blown crisis, with the recently-relegated side presently sleepwalking towards League One.

A 2-0 defeat by Birmingham at Turf Moor on Wednesday night made it 24 consecutive home league fixtures without a win for the Clarets - the longest such streak in the history of English football.

Despite this, head coach Fabio Celestini opted for the glass-half-full approach during his post-match media duties, insisting that Burnley bested Blues outside of the two boxes during the Lancashire loss.

The optimistic Swiss boss needs to increase his side's effectiveness in the decisive moments to avoid the same fate as Nicky Hayen, though, as the Clarets are winless in their opening five matches (D3 L2) with the 51-year-old at the helm.

Joining Premier League strugglers Manchester United on just the single league victory so far this season, Burnley are currently occupying 23rd position in the Championship rankings, four points from safety.

After accusing a number of his players of "not taking part in the game" at Stoke on Wednesday, it is safe to say that Millwall boss Neil is planning changes to his XI this weekend.

That indirect jab was likely commenting on the displays of Milhailo Ivanovic, Tairyk Arconte and Jenson Metcalfe, with the trio replaced at half time.

Derek Mazou-Sacko will start in the middle of the park, and influential Belgian Casper de Norre is set to return to the matchday squad.

Zak Sturge's absence reduces the hosts' options at left-back, with the 22-year-old picking up a straight red card during the defeat by Queens Park Rangers last Saturday.

Burnley also have a suspended player for this weekend's clash, with Wales international Connor Roberts out of action following his dismissal at Cardiff City on November 7.

The Clarets could make attacking alterations after firing a blank against Birmingham, with Marcus Edwards and Jamie Vardy pushing for starts.

Millwall possible starting lineup:.

Jensen; Osei-Tutu, Taylor, Cooper, Doughty; Kelly, Mazou-Sacko; Sykes, Neghli, Lisbie; Dykes.

Burnley possible starting lineup:.

Weiss; Walker, Alleyne, Julio, Pires; Cullen, Raghouber; Ramazani, Ramsey, Amdouni; Vardy.

After a soft display at Turf Moor earlier in the week, it is hard to imagine Burnley coping with the physical challenge posed by a trip to The Den.

Millwall were much-improved in the second half at Stoke and should be relatively confident of putting their relegation-threatened visitors to the sword.

Engineering signalling centres to trigger human trunk morphogenesis in vitro

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 37 min read (7381 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Vertebrate trunk development is orchestrated by endogenous signalling centres that generate gradients of signals such as WNT and BMP to pattern cell fates and drive morphogenesis1,2,3,4,5,6,7.
  • This is a preview of subscription content, access via your institution.
  • Access Nature and 54 other Nature Portfolio journals.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Vertebrate trunk development is orchestrated by endogenous signalling centres that generate gradients of signals such as WNT and BMP to pattern cell fates and drive morphogenesis1,2,3,4,5,6,7. Whether these cues alone can reconstitute human trunk-like morphogenesis in vitro remains unknown. Here we present a synthetic embryology platform for high-throughput, spatiotemporal delivery of morphogen signals to epithelial cysts derived from human pluripotent stem cells. Transient WNT and BMP gradients are sufficient to drive the generation of axially elongating trunk-like structures that contain a central neural tube flanked by axial, paraxial, intermediate and lateral mesoderm. The geometry of the transient BMP signal exerts lasting control over mediolateral patterning and bilateral symmetry. Patterning and morphogenesis are sustained by neuromesodermal and lateral plate mesoderm progenitors induced by the initial cues, which act as endogenous signalling centres. Together, these findings define a minimal spatial code sufficient to reconstitute trunk-like morphogenesis in a human stem-cell-based model and establish a scalable platform for studying early human development and congenital disorders.

GEO series are accessible at https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/ and ArrayExpress experiments at https://www.ebi.ac.uk/biostudies/arrayexpress. Raw imaging data, and any additional information required to reanalyse the data reported in this study, are available from the lead contact, S.R., on request; requests will be answered within 1 month and data shared by secure electronic file transfer without restriction. Source data are provided with this paper.

a, A detailed schematic of the workflow is shown: (i) Matrigel is microcontact printed onto the two-layered PDMS stamp (PDMS-ii) using a flat PDMS stamp (PDMS-i). (ii) A thin PDMS microwell array is peeled from the silicon master and overlaid on a glass coverslip. Taller PDMS sidewalls are plasma-bonded along two edges. (iii) Capillary water flow through the microchannels drives localized Matrigel transfer from stamp PDMS-ii onto the PDMS microwell layer at the contact interface. (iv) Cells are seeded onto the transferred Matrigel pattern, overlaid with a silanized coverslip atop the sidewalls, and cultured further with media and microwell-trapped beads. b, Photographs of the experimental setup corresponding to steps a(i–iii): coating the flat stamp (grey border, fourth column, top); PDMS-ii stamps with different patterns (blue border, first column); PDMS microwell layer with wells at different positions (red border, second column); aligned PDMS-ii stamp and PDMS microwell layer in contact (green border, third column); and the application of weight and water flow for transfer (green border, fourth column, bottom). MG, Matrigel; RT, room temperature.

It has been revealed that a–d, Design of two-layer PDMS stamp and microwell substrate: a, upper-layer pattern used to print Matrigel features; b, lower-layer embedded microchannels (white denotes channel features); c, assembled two-layer PDMS stamp with a three-dimensional illustration of the assembled stamp below; d, alignment of stamp features and microwell layer, with 120 µm diameter microwells positioned at defined distances from pattern edges. Scale bars, 1 mm. e, Whole-chip images show humidified microcontact printing (HµCP) of Matrigel mixed with fluorescently conjugated BSA (cyan) onto PDMS microwell chip (brightfield, grey), using a four-square stamp pattern. Air bubbles beneath PDMS microwell layer and above glass coverslip are visible in brightfield images. Images are representative of 6 independent experiments (12 chips) with similar results. Scale bars, 1 mm. f, Whole-chip image shows standard microcontact printing (µCP) of fluorescent BSA onto glass to validate stamp pattern from a. Image is representative of 2 independent experiments (5 chips) with similar results. Scale bar, 1 mm. g, Image shows pluripotent epithelial cysts formed 3 days after seeding on a PDMS microwell chip, using stamp pattern from a. A diversity of cyst arrangements, rather than the optimized hexagonal pattern with a central cyst as in Fig. 1, are used to show the flexibility of the approach. Image is representative of 79 independent experiments (145 chips) with similar results. Scale bar, 1 mm. h, Whole-chip epifluorescence image shows pluripotent cysts (DAPI, grey), well-trapped BMP4-coated beads (pseudocoloured red), and pSMAD1/5/9 immunofluorescence (pSMAD, green) 6 h after bead deposition. Image is representative of 6 independent experiments (13 chips) with similar results. Scale bar, 1 mm. i, Representative higher magnification images of cyst arrays with adjacent BMP beads and pSMAD1/5/9 immunofluorescence 6 h after bead deposition, from three independent experiments. (Top row) Five-cyst arrays with one or two beads, from chip in h. (Bottom left) Seven-cyst array with two beads, from an independent experiment. (Bottom right) Five-cyst array with three beads, from an independent experiment. Scale bars, 100 µm. j, (Left) Plot shows normalized pSMAD1/5/9 intensity (pSMAD/DAPI) versus distance from BMP bead, d, for all cysts from chip in h except cysts at centre of arrays (n = 201 cysts; light grey lines, individual cyst profiles; solid lines, mean; shaded areas, ±1 s.d.). (Right) pSMAD1/5/9 intensity in the bead-proximal epithelium of each cyst is plotted against the distance to the nearest bead, dmin, showing a negative correlation (red line, R2 = 0.624; n = 156 cysts) up to a distance of 635 µm, beyond which the intensity is low and uncorrelated (R2 = 0.061; n = 45 cysts). k, (Left) Normalized pSMAD1/5/9 is plotted against angle relative to bead direction (θ - θb) for cysts within responsive regime (d < 635 µm; n = 156 cysts). (Right) The direction of the pSMAD1/5/9 distribution, quantified by its first moment, is plotted as a function of the angle towards the nearest bead, θb (R2 = 0.17, n = 156 cysts). The correlation between pSMAD1/5/9 direction and bead angle is weaker than in Fig. 1f due to the overlapping influence of multiple BMP beads positioned near most cyst arrays in h.

According to recent reports, a, (top) Live YFP and merged Brightfield (BF)–YFP images show hexagonally arranged cysts derived from the BMP4-T2A-Achilles reporter hPSC line 6 h after exposure to BMP4-coated beads (pseudocoloured red), with no detectable YFP signal. Images are from one experiment (36 cyst arrays). (bottom) Live images of the cysts from (top) 24 h after bead exposure show the presence of YFP (arrowhead) in some cells adjacent to beads. Images are from one experiment (2 cyst arrays). b, Plot of BMP4 read counts per million (CPM) from bulk RNA sequencing of pluripotent cysts at 0 h, 7 h, and 24 h after BMP bead exposure (n = 3 biologically independent samples per timepoint). Dots, individual samples; bars, mean; error bars, ±1 s.d. BMP5 expression was not detected in any of the samples. c, (left) Brightfield, DAPI (grey) and definitive endoderm marker SOX17 immunofluorescence (cyan) images show spatially arranged cysts after a 2-day exposure to the main experimental conditions, including BMP bead exposure, WNT-driven symmetry breaking, and Activin/Nodal signalling inhibitor A83-01 (above), or without A83-01 (below). Images are from one experiment per condition (with A83-01: 1 chip, 21 cyst arrays; without A83-01: 2 chips, 47 cyst arrays). (right) Bulk RNA-seq analysis of key endodermal genes in cysts under the same two conditions, with (green, n = 3 biologically independent samples) or without A83-01 (purple, n = 2 biologically independent samples). Dots, individual samples; bars, mean; error bars, ±1 s.d. A83-01 prevents endoderm differentiation in all protocols here (Extended Data Fig. 5b, Fig. 4, Supplementary Data 5). d, (left) Plot of DAPI-normalized SOX2 and TBXT intensity versus distance from central cyst of array (“anterior”). TBXT varies more with distance from anterior than distance from bead (Fig. 2c) due to A–P symmetry breaking from geometric cyst arrangement16,17 (Fig. 1b). Black arrow indicates the regime where both TBXT and SOX2 are high, corresponding to NMP differentiation (n = 210 biologically independent cysts; thin lines, individual cyst profiles; thick line, mean; shaded area, 95% confidence interval). (right) Pixel density plot of normalized SOX2 versus TBXT; percentages, fractions of pixels above and below the cutoffs. 28% of pixels are SOX2+ TBXT+, indicative of NMP-like expression. e, Brightfield, DAPI (grey), and TBXT immunofluorescence (cyan) images of three hexagonal cyst arrays without (left) or with a central cyst (right) on the same chip. In the absence of the central cyst, hexagonal cysts are prone to express TBXT on both their inward- and outward-facing poles (white arrowheads), indicating a lack of clear A-P polarity. With the central cyst present, TBXT expression is restricted to the outward-facing pole. Images are representative of 2 independent experiments (12 cyst arrays) with similar results. f, Brightfield and immunofluorescence images of cysts after 2 days of differentiation show FOXF1+ nascent lateral plate mesoderm (LPM, red) proximal to BMP4-coated beads (pseudocoloured red; red arrows top left, white arrows elsewhere), whereas FOXA2+ anterior mesoderm (magenta) and SOX2+ neural progenitors (yellow) are distant from beads. Cysts are from another chip of the same design (Extended Data Fig. 2a). Images are representative of 3 independent experiments with similar results. g, Pixel-density plots of FOXA2 versus FOXF1 (top) and SOX2 versus FOXF1 (bottom) immunofluorescence in day 2 cysts, indicating mutual exclusivity. Colour, log-scaled pixel density normalized to the 99th percentile of bin density; contours, equally spaced iso-density lines; dashed lines, positivity thresholds; percentages, fraction of pixels in each quadrant. n = 7 biologically independent cysts from 3 independent experiments. h, Images of cysts after 2 days of differentiation show FOXF1+ nascent LPM located proximally to BMP beads, FOXA2+ anterior mesoderm distant from beads, and TBXT+ mesoderm at posterior end of cysts. Images are representative of 5 independent experiments with similar results. i, Per-chip fraction of cysts containing FOXF1:Achilles+ cells, plotted as in Fig. 2e, for each condition: adjacent to a BMP bead (“Bead”), no bead (“No Bead”) and adjacent to a bead following BMPR1A knockdown (“KD”). Dots, one chip from each of four independent experiments; bars, mean; error bars, ±1 s.d. across experiments. n = 182 (“Bead”), 1,010 (“No Bead”) and 189 (“KD”) cysts scored in total (see Methods, “Fraction of FOXF1+ cysts”). j, BMPR1A CPM from bulk RNA-seq of cells following BMPR1A knockdown compared with a scrambled control (n = 3 biologically independent samples per condition). Dots, individual samples; bars, mean; error bars, ±1 s.d. Two-sided Welch’s t-test: t = −7.00, d.f. = 2.5, P = 0.010, mean difference −28.1 CPM (95% CI, −42.3 to −13.9). *P < 0.05. k, Quantification of pSMAD1/5/9 in cells at the edge following 30 min treatment with 10 ng ml−1 BMP4. BMPR1A knockdown cells show reduced pSMAD1/5/9 compared with SCRAMBLE control cells (n = 3 biologically independent samples per condition). Additional quantification at different time points and cell locations is provided in Supplementary Data 4. Dots, per-well medians; centre line, median; boxes, interquartile range; whiskers, extreme values within 1.5× interquartile range. l, Representative immunostaining images for the analysis in k: BMPR1A knockdown (top row) and SCRAMBLE (bottom row); knockdown cells (CFP, yellow, left), DAPI (middle), and pSMAD1/5/9 (cyan, right). Images are from one experiment (3 wells each). m, Images show two additional replicates of day 2 morphs as in Fig. 2f, showing the co-expression of BMP4:Achilles (green) and FOXF1:mScarlet3 (red). Images are representative of 3 independent experiments (13 chips) with similar results. n, Fluorescent RNA in situ hybridization images for BMP4 (green) and FOXF1 (red) transcripts show co-localization in a bead-adjacent cyst after 2 days of differentiation. Representative image from n = 6 biologically independent bead-adjacent cysts. o, Pixel-density plot of FOXF1 versus BMP4 in situ signal in the day 2 cyst shown in n. Colour, log-scaled pixel density normalized to its maximum; contours, equally spaced iso-density lines. The two signals are positively correlated (R2 = 0.646). Scale bars, 100 µm.

a, A schematic of trunk morph differentiation protocol is shown. hPSCs were seeded onto micropatterned PDMS microwell substrate on Day −3 in mTeSR Plus with 10 µM Y-27632. The next day, Y-27632 was removed from media conditions and Matrigel added to induce the formation of single lumen epithelial cysts. On Day 0, BMP4-coated beads were injected into microwells, and cyst differentiation was initiated in N2B27 with 8–10 µM CHIR99021, 0.1–0.15 µM A83-01, and 50 ng ml−1 NOGGIN. After 48 h, cysts were transferred to individual wells in N2B27 with Matrigel and cultured for 3–4 days before analysis. b, Box-and-whisker plots show length of trunk morphs at 0, 48, and 120 h of differentiation. The same n = 93 biologically independent trunk morph samples were tracked across all three time points. Centre line, median; boxes, 25th-75th percentile; whiskers, 1.5 × the interquartile range beyond the quartiles; dots, individual trunk morphs. c, (left) Box-and-whisker plots of trunk morph length on days 3, 4 and 5 without (red, n = 10 biologically independent trunk morph samples) or with the WNT-secretion inhibitor IWP3 (green, n = 8 biologically independent trunk morph samples), added after 48 h; each morph was tracked across all three time points. Centre line, median; boxes, 25th-75th percentile; whiskers, 1.5 × the interquartile range beyond the quartiles; dots, individual trunk morphs. Differences between conditions at each time point were assessed using two-sided Mann–Whitney U tests with Bonferroni correction for multiple comparisons; Hodges-Lehmann median differences are given with Bonferroni-adjusted (98.3%) confidence intervals. Day 3: U = 16, P = 0.103, −59 µm (−160 to 18). Day 4: U = 4, P = 1.6 × 10−3, −212 µm (−314 to −100). Day 5: U = 0, P = 1.4 × 10−4, −353 µm (−438 to −287). ns, P > 0.05; **, P < 0.01; ***, P < 0.001. (Right) Fluorescent RNA in situ hybridization images for WNT3A (left, green) and WNT5A (right, magenta) transcripts, together with brightfield imaging, show WNT ligand expression at the posterior end (n = 5 biologically independent trunk morph samples per probe, from 2 independent experiments). d, Representative epifluorescence images of trunk morphs after transient BMP4-bead exposure show FOXF1+ lateral plate mesoderm (cyan) bilaterally (left), unilaterally (middle), and posteriorly localized (right). Images are representative of 3 independent experiments (11 chips, 93 trunk morphs scored across all bead configurations) with similar results. e, Representative images of day 5 trunk morphs following transient exposure to medially positioned BMP4-coated beads. Posterior-restricted LPM was observed only at bead-cyst distances below 160 µm (5 of 12 morphs); all 9 trunk morphs with larger distances highlighted bilateral FOXF1. Images are from one experiment (3 chips, 21 trunk morphs). f-g, Representative images of trunk morphs exposed to (f) a unilateral bead or (g) two bilateral beads show unilateral or bilateral FOXF1, respectively. MESP2:mCherry is bilateral in all morphs. Images are representative of the same experiments and morphs as in d. h, Confocal images show DAPI (grey), MESP2:mCherry (red), phalloidin (grey), and FOXF1 (cyan) in a trunk morph. Single lumen, polarized somites (white arrows) are visible within the single focal plane. Man Utd transfer news: Sporting CP star 'wants to join' Old Trafford as asking price now revealed

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (421 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Lewis Blain | 26 Nov 2026 12:28.
  • Manchester United have been handed a potential boost in their pursuit of Sporting CP left-back Maxi Araujo, who is reportedly keen on a move to Old Trafford.
  • The Uruguay international caught the attention of United officials during Wednesday's 2-2 draw in Lisbon, having been monitored by the club for several months.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Lewis Blain | 26 Nov 2026 12:28.

Manchester United have been handed a potential boost in their pursuit of Sporting CP left-back Maxi Araujo, who is reportedly keen on a move to Old Trafford.

The Uruguay international caught the attention of United officials during Wednesday's 2-2 draw in Lisbon, having been monitored by the club for several months.

However, a potential January deal could prove difficult given the asking price and Mauricio Pochettino's limited transfer budget.

According to Sport Witness, a source close to the situation has indicated that Araujo 'wants to join' United, with mutual appreciation between the player and the Premier League outfit.

United first indicated interest in the 26-year-old earlier this year but failed to strengthen at left-back during the summer. Araujo subsequently extended his Sporting contract until 2030, which includes an €80m (£67m) release clause.

However, it's believed a fee closer to £50m could actually be enough to secure his services in the January transfer window, despite his newly introduced contract and substantial salary in Portugal.

United officials reportedly watched him closely during Wednesday's Champions League meeting, with Araujo playing the full 90 minutes.

The left-back has made 15 appearances this season and is viewed as a potential solution to United's problems in the position.

Luke Shaw has missed the last eight matches with a muscle injury, while youngster Harry Amass is also among the club's recognised options. Both players have contracts expiring in 2027, adding further uncertainty to the position.

Araujo's performance against United offered Pochettino an opportunity to assess a potential transfer target at close quarters.

It has been revealed that operating in an advanced left wing-back role, the Uruguayan registered two shots, created one chance, won three fouls and completed six progressive passes. He also made six defensive contributions, including three interceptions, per Sofascore.

It was not necessarily a spectacular individual display, but his all-round contribution attracted praise from the Portuguese press and demonstrated the qualities United could benefit from on the left flank.

Araujo could provide the attacking thrust and defensive work rate required to solve a problem position, although the financial implications are significant.

A reported £50m asking price would represent a sizeable investment, particularly with United believed to have less than that available for multiple positions in January.

Pochettino may be impressed by what he saw in Lisbon, but convincing the hierarchy to spend such a large proportion of their budget on one full-back could be difficult when central defence and striker reinforcements are also needed.

Exercise coaching boosts colon cancer survival

📅 06 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1014 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In 2025, an international trial found that people treated for colon cancer were more likely to be alive eight years later if they had received long-term exercise coaching.
  • The question facing doctors now is less whether people with cancer should exercise, and rather how they should build it into routine care.
  • Yet experts caution that the trial's findings may not apply to every cancer or every patient.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In 2025, an international trial found that people treated for colon cancer were more likely to be alive eight years later if they had received long-term exercise coaching.

The question facing doctors now is less whether people with cancer should exercise, and rather how they should build it into routine care. In the US, that shift is reaching hospital standards. From January 2027, breast cancer centers must screen patients' physical function and recommend exercise or physical therapy where needed.

Yet experts caution that the trial's findings may not apply to every cancer or every patient.

The 2025 trial, called CHALLENGE, was led by the Canadian Cancer Trials Group. It began enrolling patients in 2009 and published its results in 2025.

The trial's 889 participants came from six countries, most from Canada and Australia. All had finished surgery and chemotherapy for stage 2 or 3 colon cancer, which had not spread to distant organs.

In a recent development, half received only health education materials on exercise and healthy eating. The other half additionally met a physical activity consultant for three years.

In the exercise group, the target was similar to adding 45 to 60 minutes of brisk walking, three to four times a week. The amount and type of activity varied from person to person, said Tormod Skogstad Nilsen, a cancer exercise researcher in Norway. But he said participants achieved lasting increases in their physical activity.

Recent findings suggest that exercise helped. People in the exercise group were less likely to see their cancer come back, to develop a fresh cancer or to die. In all, 93 had at least one of these setbacks, compared with 131 in the health education group.

Industry observers note that in cancer research, living longer usually means a larger share of people is still alive at a given point. It does not promise anyone a set number of extra years.

Eight years after joining CHALLENGE, about 90 of every 100 people in the exercise group were alive, compared with about 83 of every 100 in the health education group. That is about 7% more people alive in the group who had guided exercise.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

For people without cancer, the evidence comes from studies that follow people's habits and health over many years. These can show a link, but not prove cause and effect. Active people may also eat better or smoke less.

In another 2025 study, more than 85,000 adults in the United Kingdom wore a wrist tracker for a week. Over about six years, those who moved most had a 26% lower risk of 13 cancers, including breast and colorectal cancer, than those who moved least.

Industry observers note that even light activity, such as household chores, was linked to lower risk. The link held after researchers accounted for lifestyle, weight and other health conditions.

Earlier research, based on people's self-reporting, has led to similar conclusions. A 2016 analysis of 1.44 million adults in the US and Europe linked free-time activity to a lower risk of many cancers, largely regardless of weight or smoking.

A trial to prove prevention is unlikely: Many cancers take years to develop, so it would need huge numbers of people followed for a long time.

According to recent reports, CHALLENGE included only people with colon cancer. But how it picked participants offers a clue: Before joining, they had to pass a fitness test.

Anna Campbell, a professor of clinical exercise science at Edinburgh Napier University in Scotland, sees that as a guide.

Sources indicate that "I think patients with any other cancer stage II and III who have a reasonable baseline level of fitness and no major comorbidities that would prevent them from undertaking moderate to vigorous activity could be considered for similar interventions," she remarked. Comorbidities are other health conditions.

Nilsen noted some people decline to join exercise trials because they feel too unwell or tired, or do not want to exercise. "Hence, study populations are typically younger, 'healthier', and most times slightly more motivated compared to a clinical population," he noted.

The coaching aimed to make activity a lasting habit, and Campbell said that is where the trial's value lies.

"The main success of the study is that it enabled the participants to become independent exercisers staying active in a safe and effective and individualized way," she mentioned.

It has been revealed that nilsen agreed. Helping people become more active "in their own environment," without depending on a well-equipped training center, "would likely lead to more sustainable activity behavioral changes," he said.

It has been revealed that he is wary of fixed targets, however. "Exercise should be tailored to each individual and the challenges they face, rather than striving to reach a given minimum of exercise required," though health care resources may not always allow it, he added.

In a 2024 survey of 549 people with cancer, only one in 10 had been referred to an exercise service. Yet almost three in four thought their oncologist should raise the subject.

"There are some excellent examples of effective pathways but these are few and far between," said Campbell. Good services bring everyone on board, from surgeons to community fitness instructors.

"Ideally, one person in the clinical setting needs to champion the program to link all the team together.".

Campbell expects CHALLENGE's regular coaching will be cut back in everyday care. Apps and live online group sessions could still work, she noted, if run by properly trained staff.

One recent study of live online exercise engaged patients from poorer backgrounds, in rural areas and with advanced cancer. "It answered some of the barriers, such as cost, travel and lack of confidence," she said.

Patients can ask their care team what exercise is safe for them and what support exists.

According to Nilsen, a training session can bring structure and tech giant. "You made it here, despite your feeling unwell or fatigued this morning, so you feel mastery based on that," he said.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

This season’s Premier League title race may be locked in a paralysed state of uncertainty but Arsenal, the defending champions, are determined to keep it interesting.

While the painful delay on Manchester City’s battle against their guilty verdict threatens to drag deep into next year, Arsenal are remaining hot on their tails.

City’s lead at the top is back to three points but Arsenal’s win here was unlikely to have sent any shivers down the spines of Enzo Maresca and his players in this phoney mess of a season.

It was not until the 80th minute that Arsenal finally registered their first shot on target, and that was the moment which ended their cycle of frustration at the City Ground.

Just when it appeared Mikel Arteta was heading for a third successive goalless draw at the home of Nottingham Forest, substitute Noni Madueke’s deflected strike proved the difference.

Noni Madueke breaks the deadlock at the City Ground! 🔓 https://t.co/RdL48f3OLC.

Trips to the City Ground have rarely been easy for Arsenal, with an FA Cup defeat in January 2022, at a time when Forest were still in the Championship, sparking a famous Arteta rant in the dressing room which was included in the All Or Nothing documentary.

They were far from fluent here and have now failed to score in the first half of their last six Premier League and Champions League matches.

Recent findings suggest that eberechi Eze endured a particularly difficult afternoon in what was a missed opportunity for the England international, with Madueke replacing him at half-time. Yet Arteta will argue that finding a way to win games when not at their best is a sign of champions.

Sources indicate that “We have played 11 competitive matches and won 10 of them, we are in a good place and will improve,” Arteta said. “Since losing at Brighton we have won three games in a row so that is the response that I want.

“The level of the league has gone up again and there will be more and more surprises. We have to go again at Bayern Munich this week [in the Champions League on Wednesday night] and we will have to adapt to that one too.

“I have a smile on my face as Noni is a special guy. He’s in a good moment and after the [international] break he’s shown another level. The team needs him and he’s doing well.”.

Arsenal often struggled against teams who operate with a compact midfield and defend deeply last season and this was another case in point.

When Declan Rice wastefully lifted a shot over the crossbar 18 minutes from the end, after a rare opening in the Forest area, it did appear that another draw was inevitable.

Madueke has struggled for consistency and minutes since his £52m move from Chelsea, so this felt like a big moment for the winger.

According to recent reports, “If you look at the quality of our starting XI and bench it’s absurd,” Madueke said. “We have elite players of the highest level and it’s great to have that type of competition. You know on the bench that you’re ready to have an impact. We showed grit and determination and showed a champion spirit.”.

They have only recorded two home wins in the league over the past 11 months which, quite frankly, is relegation form.

They did not deserve to lose this match. Without their injured talisman Morgan Gibbs-White, Forest defended resolutely and in the second half displayed far more attacking impetus without ever truly testing Arsenal goalkeeper David Raya.

Liam Delap, their £50m record signing, produced a fine centre-forward performance and never allowed Arsenal’s centre-backs Ezri Konsa and Gabriel to feel comfortable. Goals, however, continue to elude this team.

Glasner remarked: “I feel really sorry for the players because we didn’t deserve that.

“It feels unfair but I don’t want to be complaining as we are the only ones who can change it.

It has been revealed that “It is a tough moment and we need to stick together and stay positive. Sometimes it takes a while – during my first year at Palace we didn’t start well but we had a turnaround.

“We are playing better right now but we also concede how competitive the Premier League is because every mistake you get punished.”.

Now it is how we deal with the situation and react as a team and just how we can change this is by staying positive, sticking together and working hard.

In honour of nine-year-old Forest fan James Kerry, who died earlier this month of cancer.

We'll wear black armbands this afternoon, as we join our hosts in remembering nine-year-old Nottingham Forest supporter, James Kerry, who passed away earlier this month following a brave battle with cancer. Rest in peace, James ❤️ https://t.co/YFIXnCfJJX.

Surely we cannot have another 0-0 in this fixture? Looking at the talent in Arsenal’s front third, and the fact they are playing their two most offensive full-backs, this might be more open than assummed.

Arsenal can cut Manchester City’s lead to three points with a win today but does it all matter?

Manchester City’s battle against their guilty verdict is threatening to run into next year and this title race feels fake and damaged.

It is a sham of a season with the prospect of asterisks all over the Premier League campaign.

Arsenal can only carry on as normal as they defend their title but this is an unsatisfactory mess.

The margins are really small and it’s a team and a manager that we know really well, extraordinary manager, really well organised.

They are dangerous in many areas, a very well set-up team and you need to be very tight, very neat, very efficient in everything that you do. You have to insist and insist, and then there’s a lot of volume of actions.

[On coming from behind] Yes, and it’s part of the game, your capacity when something doesn’t go as planned to react and still win the game, and we know the challenge that we have here. In the last two years, we haven’t been able to win here and that’s an opportunity as well to show what we are made of.

Another reason Arsenal will be feeling confident today is Forest’s abysmal home form in the Premier League.

It may surprise neutrals outside of Nottingham but results at the City Ground have been poor for some time.

Indeed, it is just two league wins in 11 months in front of their own supporters which, quite frankly, is relegation form.

In a recent development, before this game, Forest’s head coach Oliver Glasner said: “We have to change it. I spoke to one or two experienced lads who know Forest better than I do and talked about the situation. But if you always talk about the problem it makes it bigger and bigger.

“We haven’t scored a goal at home yet or won a game at home, and that is what we have to change.”.

Trips to the City Ground have seldom been easy for Mikel Arteta, with two successive 0-0 draws in the Premier League.

An FA Cup defeat in Jan 2022, at a time when Forest were still in the Championship, sparked a famous Arteta rant in the dressing room which was included in the All Or Nothing documentary.

Yet Arsenal have secured two wins in a row since that defeat at Brighton, without being truly at their fluent best, and will be confident against a Forest team without injured talisman Morgan Gibbs-White.

Eze over Madueke and Guimaraes over Lewis-Skelly were closer calls for Arteta. Ben White comes in for Timber, with Arsenal managing the minutes of both right-backs.

Germán Castaños, an expert in innovation who has written multiple books on alternative thinking, has become a key member of the team. Things started with a phone call with Nicolas Jover, then a meeting with Arteta and now he splits his time between Argentina and London. Find out more about Arsenal’s mystery man and his methods here.

In the ordinary course of a Premier League season, you would say Manchester City have applied pressure on Arsenal by opening up a six-point lead before the champions play at Nottingham Forest this afternoon.

This is not a normal Premier League season though, and we await to discover if the top of the league table is simply a mirage.

Regardless, Mikel Arteta and his Arsenal players have their own motivations to accumulate as many points as possible before January as they seek to retain the title for the first time since the 1930s.

Arsenal have struggled at the City Ground, drawing 0-0 on their last two Premier League visits. They also lost at Forest in May 2023, a result which confirmed Manchester City as champions at Arsenal’s expense, and were knocked out of the FA Cup by Forest in January 2022.

Forest are yet to score a home league goal under Oliver Glasner, another data point suggesting this will be a low-scoring game.

That might not be the full story though, with Forest creating a hatful of chances in their defeat at Crystal Palace last week and Arsenal also playing a more inventive, technical game with the ball so far this season.

Arsenal have yet to score from a non-penalty set-piece, and their percentage of goals from open play is now the highest in the Premier League.

It has been revealed that morgan Gibbs-White is a doubt after sustaining what Glasner described as a “minor muscle injury” at Palace and his involvement in the game will be a last-minute call. With the exception of Christos Tzolis, Piero Hincapie and long-term absentee William Saliba, Arsenal’s squad is in pretty good health. Bukayo Saka, Martin Odegaard, Kai Havertz, Riccardo Calafiori and Ben White could be recalled to Arteta’s starting XI after starting the Champions League win over Lille on the bench.

Preston North End play host to Norwich City on Saturday afternoon looking for the win that could move them outside of the relegation zone.

At a time when the home side sit in 22nd place in the Championship table, Norwich remain in 11th position despite their prolonged unbeaten streak.

While many questioned why Graham Alexander left a League One promotion bid with Bradford for a relegation scrap at Deepdale, the Preston legend is presently justifying his decision.

Seven points have been accumulated across the last three fixtures against Southampton, West Ham United and Cardiff City.

Preston had been heavy underdogs in all three contests, yet they came through that triple-header having conceded just the one goal.

Although Preston had to battle hard to earn a share of the spoils at West Ham on Saturday, they were ruthless in dispatching Cardiff by a 4-0 scoreline in South Wales three days later.

Despite remaining three points adrift of safety, confidence is growing at Preston ahead of facing one of the form teams in the division.

Such has been the upturn in Norwich's fortunes that they were disappointed to record a 1-1 draw at home to Queens Park Rangers in midweek.

Nevertheless, having won their previous five games, it extended their recent return to 16 points from a possible 18.

Philippe Clement's side remain with three points of sixth-placed Southampton, a position they will take having lost eight of their opening 11 league matches this season.

Norwich have scored 19 goals in eight away fixtures, the joint-best attacking record in the division, while they have won their most recent three contests away from Carrow Road.

Norwich City Championship form:.

Barring any fitness issues, Preston boss Alexander is expected to name the same starting lineup from the Cardiff game.

Preston were 4-0 ahead before substitutions were first made in the 77th minute, and the same players should keep their places.

The likes of Harry Clarke, Lewis Gibson and Liam Gibbs are all expected to remain sidelined.

Meanwhile, Kenny McLean, Anis Ben Slimane, Oscar Schwartau and Jovon Makama are all in contention for opportunities in the Norwich XI.

Jacob Wright, Paris Maghoma and Mathias Kvistgaarden could be the players to drop down to the substitutes' bench.

Preston North End possible starting lineup:.

Nicholls; Hughes, Lindsay, Offiah; Mills, Thompson, Docherty, Small; Devine, Moran; Burgzorg.

Norwich City possible starting lineup:.

Grimshaw; Stacey, Darling, McConville, Yongwa; Field, McLean; Brooks, Ven Slimane, Musaba; Makama.

Although Preston recorded the most eye-catching Championship result in midweek, it remains to be seen whether they can back that up against a team playing with Norwich's confidence. Therefore, we are backing the Canaries to come out on top, albeit in a match where Preston will continue to show their improvements under Alexander.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Lewis Blain | 26 Nov 2026 12:48.

Chelsea have joined Tottenham Hotspur in keeping tabs on emerging France international Sael Kumbedi, who is attracting growing interest from a host of Premier League clubs.

The 21-year-old defender has enjoyed a rapid rise in Germany, with his recent senior international breakthrough further enhancing his reputation.

Xabi Alonso is among several managers who appear to be assessing the versatile VfL Wolfsburg defender ahead of a potential transfer.

The Blues, Tottenham and Fulham are all 'monitoring' Kumbedi, while City Football Group have also been tracking his progress throughout the campaign, according to TEAMtalk.

The right-back moved to Germany from Lyon in August 2025, initially joining Wolfsburg on loan before the Bundesliga club activated their €6m purchase option.

Despite Wolfsburg suffering relegation to Bundesliga 2, Kumbedi opted to remain with the club and help them pursue an immediate return to the German top-flight.

His decision has not prevented his reputation from growing, with Zinedine Zidane handing him his first senior France call-up earlier this month following an injury withdrawal from the squad.

Kumbedi made his international debut against Italy at San Siro on November 12th, becoming the first Bundesliga 2 player to receive a France senior call-up since David Trezeguet in 2007.

Chelsea's interest in Kumbedi could make sense given the uncertainty surrounding their options at right-back.

Reece James' injury problems have created a significant headache for Alonso, with Pedro Neto having been deployed in a wing-back role and centre-back Josh Acheampong also shifted out to the right.

Malo Gusto's uncertain future at Stamford Bridge is another potential consideration, leaving Chelsea with reasons to explore the market for a specialist defender capable of providing greater depth and versatility.

European scouts are reportedly impressed by his pace, athleticism and stamina, while his ability to operate on either flank further adds to his appeal.

That versatility is particularly attractive to a side like Chelsea, who are seeking defensive reinforcements in 2027, with the French gem's performances over the coming months likely to remain under close scrutiny.

However, the west London side are not alone in their interest, with top-flight rivals Spurs, Fulham and City also monitoring the Frenchman.

His international breakthrough could make competition for his signature increasingly fierce, but Chelsea's need for greater stability and depth on the right makes this a potential transfer worth watching.

American soccer stat Trinity Rodman has backed out of the USWNT roster for the 2026 CONCACAF W Championship taking place beginning later this week.

The announcement comes hours after the Daily Mail was first to report her split from longtime boyfriend and tennis star Ben Shelton.

US Soccer says Rodman suffered 'a minor shoulder injury' in the 2026 NWSL Championship.

Despite multiple sacrifices and last-minute trips to attend each other's matches, it appears they could no longer make it work.

The same evening, Rodman, 24, and the Washington Spirit lost the NWSL final to the KC Current.

The following evening, the American tennis star was spotted at Madison Square Garden for the Fresh York Knicks' game against the Indiana Pacers without Rodman, instead sitting on Celebrity Row alongside a friend and actress Inde Navarette.

The couple first went public with their relationship in March 2025 following speculation from fans.

Mystery surrounded the early stages of their relationship, as they initially dropped a playful hint as part of a TikTok trend last March then 'hard released' their romance soon afterwards.

Their conflicting work schedules made it too challenging to maintain their relationship.

The sporting power couple went public with their relationship around March 2025.

Breaking: What to know about the IIHF Women's Ice Hockey World Championship

📅 06 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (598 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that since its inception in 1990, the Women's Ice Hockey World Championship has almost always been held in the spring — apart from 2021 and 2022, when the COVID-19 pandemic saw it moved to the summer.
  • According to recent reports, the idea is make it easier for all of the world's best players to participate.
  • Industry observers note that "This gives the women's game a unique selling point," International Ice Hockey Federation (IIHF) President Franz Reindl recently told the SID news agency.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that since its inception in 1990, the Women's Ice Hockey World Championship has almost always been held in the spring — apart from 2021 and 2022, when the COVID-19 pandemic saw it moved to the summer. This year, though, the tournament, being hosted by Denmark from November 6 to November 16, is being held in November for the first time.

According to recent reports, the idea is make it easier for all of the world's best players to participate. Since its inception in 2023, the North America-based Professional Women's Hockey League (PWHL), widely considered the world's best, has had to pause its season to allow players to take part in the Worlds. This is no longer necessary, as the PWHL's regular season doesn't open until December.

Industry observers note that "This gives the women's game a unique selling point," International Ice Hockey Federation (IIHF) President Franz Reindl recently told the SID news agency. "Because the PWHL season begins after this, we can be certain that the very best players are participating.".

Recent findings suggest that previously, the teams were divided into a stronger group and a weaker group, with the idea being to avoid, as much as possible, lopsided scores. This is because women's hockey is not as balanced as the men's game, with Canada or the United States having won every tournament since its inception.

Under the old system, all five teams in the stronger Group A advanced to the quarterfinals. Under the newly introduced format, four of the five teams advance from both groups. This also sees powerhouses the US and Canada in separate groups, meaning the marquee matchup can't occur early in the tournament.

Group A: USA, Czechia, Switzerland, Germany, Austria.

Group B: Canada, Finland, Sweden, Japan, Denmark.

It has been revealed that no. While the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) ruled on October 30 — a week before the opening faceoff of the Women's Ice Hockey World Championship — that the IIHF must allow Russia back into its tournaments during the 2026-2027 season, it made no mention of this tournament. Under the CAS ruling though, the IIHF will be required to include Russia at the 2027 tournament in Quebec City.

Recent findings suggest that as noted above, either Canada or the United States has won every edition of this tournament — and indeed the two countries have split Olympic gold medals between them (Canada with five, USA with three) since the sport was introduced to the Winter Games in 1998. There is nothing to suggest that this is about to change in Herning and Esbjerg, although Canada enters the tournament with a vastly different roster from the one that won Olympic silver in Milano in February.

Among those looking to break this North American domination are Finland, the only other team ever to have made it to a world championship final and Switzerland, who took bronze in Milan.

The United States and Canada will play in generic kits provided by the International Ice Hockey Federation's official supplier due to an ongoing commercial rights dispute.

The Canadian federation, Hockey Canada, said in a statement on Wednesday that its players would be wearing jerseys designed by True Hockey instead of their Bauer jerseys featuring the national team logo. USA Hockey has confirmed that its players too will be wearing jerseys without its national emblem.

"While we have yet to see the jersey Canada will be playing in on Friday, our team remains focused on the tournament and representing our country proudly on and off the ice," Hockey Canada said.

By Darren Plant | 26 Nov 2026 12:49.

Derby County and Watford square off at Pride Park on Saturday afternoon as two of the worst performing teams in the division.

While the Rams sit at the bottom of the Championship table, Watford are only five points ahead of them and with a head coach taking charge of his first Hornets match.

When Derby travelled to Molineux to face Wolverhampton Wanderers on Tuesday night, they would not have necessarily expected to earn anything from one of the form teams in the division.

However, despite having troubled Wolves during the opening half hour, the Rams succumbed to a 3-0 defeat and allowed their opponents to have the most shots (39) by any team in the Championship in 11 years.

John Eustace has now overseen 11 defeats in 17 league matches, and it is realistic to assume that he may be sacked if Derby lose this game.

In four of their last eight outings, Derby have conceded at least three goals, while they have only netted more than once in a fixture in 13 outings.

On a positive note, the East Midlands outfit did win their last contest at Pride Park, overcoming Bolton Wanderers by a 3-1 scoreline on November 6.

Meanwhile, Watford head into this encounter with former Romania and Legia Warsaw boss Edward Iordanescu in the dugout for his first game in English football.

The Hornets have accumulated seven points from seven matches, hardly a disaster at this stage of the season.

Nevertheless, back-to-back defeats have been posted at Sheffield United and against Blackburn Rovers without scoring a goal.

Despite holding leaders Middlesbrough to a goalless draw before the November international break, Watford have now failed to score in three successive matches.

Furthermore, they have collected just one point from eight away matches this season, that 1-1 draw at Wrexham in August being followed by seven consecutive defeats on their travels.

Derby County Championship form:.

Oscar Fraulo and Bobby Clark are both pushing for a return to the Derby midfield.

Jack Robinson may return to the defence, whether that be as a central defender in a back three or left-back in a back four.

Eustace must decide whether to use Rhian Brewster in an unfamiliar wing-back role for the second game in a row, but Sammie Szmodics remains in a packed treatment room.

Iordanescu will be forced into at least two Watford changes through Mattie Pollock and Jordan Zemura serving suspensions.

Branimir Mlacic and Marc Bola appear likely to deputise, while Edo Kayembe, Rocco Vata and Othmane Maamma will also be considered for opportunities further up the pitch.

Derby County possible starting lineup:.

Widell-Zetterstrom; Clarke, Sanderson, Robinson; Nyambe, Ozoh, Mowatt, Clark, Brewster; Fuseini, Morris.

Watford possible starting lineup:.

Ravaglia; Traore, Mlacic, Coulibaly, Bola; Kayembe, Kyprianou, Bravo; Vata, Doumbia, Maamma.

Industry observers note that with Watford transitioning to a newly introduced head coach, it is difficult to predict how they may perform. Nevertheless, this is a must-win match for Derby and Eustace, and we are backing the Rams to net a late goal to edge this contest.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Matthew Cooper | 26 Nov 2026 12:57.

MK Dons will be looking to continue their good form when they welcome Notts County to Stadium MK on Saturday.

The hosts presently sit 10th in the League One table, while the visitors are 19th.

MK Dons have found some form in recent weeks after making a poor start to the season and are unbeaten in their last five league games heading into Saturday's fixture.

Paul Warne's side failed to win any of their first eight league matches, but have now won five of their last seven after picking up their first victory over Luton back in October.

The Dons won four successive league games, scoring a whopping 17 goals in the process, before being held to a 1-1 draw by Mansfield Town last Saturday.

Michael Smith put Mansfield ahead in the first half, but Callum Paterson rescued a late draw for MK Dons with a headed goal in the 80th minute.

However, it is worth noting that MK Dons have failed to beat Notts County in their last six meetings across all competitions.

Notts County are looking to get back to winning ways after suffering a narrow 1-0 home defeat to Stevenage last weekend.

The Magpies should have taken the lead after they were awarded a penalty late in the game, but Conor Grant's effort was saved by Tommy Setford before Josh Magennis scored the winner for Stevenage in the 86th minute.

That defeat leaves Martin Paterson's side with 14 points from 13 matches, with the head coach describing the defeat as a "hammer blow" and admitting his side are "not good enough to have a day off".

Paterson will be hoping for a response against MK Dons this weekend, knowing that Notts County could slip into the relegation zone if they lose and results elsewhere go against them.

Notts County form (all competitions):.

Paterson is expected to start up front after scoring against Mansfield and he will likely be partnered by Aaron Collins, who is the division's leading scorer with 13 goals from 14 games.

Dan Crowley, Ryan Wintle and Alex Gilbey are set to continue in midfield.

Notts County are expected to stick with Daniel Kanu as their lone striker, having scored twice in his last four league appearances.

Scott Robertson and Dean Campbell are likely to start in midfield, with Callum Roberts and Luka Smyth featuring further forward.

Dennis; Ekpiteta, Goode, Sanders; Silvera, Crowley, Wintle, Gilbey, Campbell; Paterson, Collins.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It seems we are heading into the final year of Fikayo Tomori’s playing relationship with AC Milan, with talk of a renewal silent.

Next year, at the end of June, Tomori’s deal expires and if nothing is done before then, his six-year spell with the club will come to an end.

Industry observers note that read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

It has been revealed that it’s been an up-and-down season for the Englishman, especially after he was included in the ‘bomb squad’ through the mercato. However, he was needed back in the squad and reintegrated.

Recent findings suggest that despite showing this fight, though, it seems unlikely that he’ll be rewarded with a new deal. There are prepares to invest heavily in the club next year and the defender isn’t seen as a pillar of the team, let alone the defence. So a renewal isn’t being focused on.

In a recent development, as Matteo Moretto told viewers on Fabrizio Romano’s YouTube channel, Tomori previously had a chance at a renewal. However, that now seems to have gone, as MilanNews relays.

According to recent reports, “There’s a before and after regarding Tomori. In my opinion, if Massimiliano Allegri had remained on the Milan bench, perhaps in that case there could have been a chance of a renewal for Tomori.

“Then there was the slightly peculiar way Milan handled the Tomori situation. Tomori is a player who has always been absolutely professional and deeply loves the Milan shirt; he has always shown all his commitment.

“It’s true, he was sidelined; Milan tried to find solutions on the way out right in the last days of the transfer window. His contract expires in 2027.

“There were discussions underway for the renewal when Allegri was on the bench; then, with time and with the succession of certain events, this type of renewal was no longer discussed.

“To date, the negotiations are absolutely at a standstill. There is no dialogue between the parties and I repeat, Tomori’s contract expires in 2027.

“We’ll see if in January there can be a way out, perhaps with the payment of compensation to Milan, or if it will reach zero in June, but as of today there is no trace of a possible renewal.”.
