Preparing for 45C: How Germany tests its crisis response

📅 05 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (750 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Imagine a situation in which prolonged drought has devastated Germany and much of Europe, taking a toll on people's lives, the environment and economy — with a heat wave with temperatures of up to 45 degrees Celsius (113 degrees Fahrenheit) compounding the situation.
  • About 180 organizations across Germany, including more than 60 ministries at the state level and nearly 20 federal authorities, are taking part in a major crisis exercise known as LÜKEX 26, which is built around this very scenario.
  • Recent findings suggest that it is Germany's cross-government crisis management exercise organized by the Federal Office of Civil Protection and Disaster Assistance (BBK).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Imagine a situation in which prolonged drought has devastated Germany and much of Europe, taking a toll on people's lives, the environment and economy — with a heat wave with temperatures of up to 45 degrees Celsius (113 degrees Fahrenheit) compounding the situation.

About 180 organizations across Germany, including more than 60 ministries at the state level and nearly 20 federal authorities, are taking part in a major crisis exercise known as LÜKEX 26, which is built around this very scenario.

Recent findings suggest that it is Germany's cross-government crisis management exercise organized by the Federal Office of Civil Protection and Disaster Assistance (BBK). And it's been up and running for more than two decades.

Industry observers note that the first LÜKEX in 2004 dealt with the scenario of an extreme winter with a major power outage. Lessons from that exercise proved valuable in 2005 when the Münsterland region of North Rhine-Westphalia — Germany's most populous state — experienced the worst power outage in the country's postwar history. When heavy snowfall caused power lines to collapse, leaving 250,000 people without electricity for days, there was a better understanding of who to contact and where the bottlenecks were.

Sources indicate that since it first started, LÜKEX has trained for scenarios involving terror attacks, an influenza pandemic, biological health threats, storm floods in northern Germany and gas shortages in southern Germany. The most recent exercise in 2023 simulated a cyberattack targeting government operations.

With the help of other ministries, the German Weather Service and the Federal Institute of Hydrology, the BBK developed a drought risk analysis to serve as the scenario.

Participants, which include aid organizations Malteser and the German Red Cross, didn't know the specifics of the challenges they would be facing until the exercise kicked off on Wednesday.

It has been revealed that at that point, they were told it was July 20, 2027. In that simulated future, they find themselves in a Germany that has been struggling with extreme heat for weeks; water levels in rivers are falling, food supplies are becoming scarce and emergency services are under growing pressure.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Patrick Pöhler, spokesperson for Malteser, noted additional details include supermarkets having run out of water, collapsed supply chains and skyrocketing prices to enter a swimming pool. He said the scenario also goes into how the situation is impacting sections of society.

In a recent development, "Emergency services and elderly care are areas that require particular attention," Pöhler said. "The increasingly extreme summers of recent years have shown how severely heat can affect staffing levels and operational capacity.".

In its scenario, the northern port city of Hamburg is tasked with managing the disruption of key transport routes that are impacting access to food and drinking water, as well as handling disinformation attacks that are fueling public fear.

According to recent reports, "We have not conducted an exercise of this magnitude since the end of the Cold War. Yet such preparations are essential to strengthen our resilience and crisis-response capabilities," remarked Hamburg's minister for the interior, Andy Grote.

LÜKEX is designed to test and strengthen the country's ability to manage major crises at a strategic level. No matter the specific scenario, they all help test internal structures, workflows and decision-making processes.

"The lessons learned are continuously incorporated into improving preparedness, planning and cooperation in civil protection," noted BBK spokesperson Katharina Böcker.

This year's topic was decided a long time ago, well before recent summers in which Germany experienced extreme heat, she added. Thousands of people died from heat-related causes during the hot months of this year.

"Crises such as extreme heat waves and prolonged droughts can affect large parts of the population and challenge the operational capabilities of our critical structures over an extended period," noted Christian Reuter, secretary general of the German Red Cross, another organization taking part.

Observers take note of how organizations react in the crisis scenario to find out what went well and where things didn't run smoothly.

"We are explicitly encouraged to make mistakes," said Malteser's Pöhler, because that is how weaknesses can be identified and addressed.

A first internal debrief is scheduled for Friday, he added.

A preliminary report with the main findings and respective recommendations is due to be published in the first quarter of next year. A full evaluation report will then be released later in the third quarter of 2027.

#153621. De novo design of high-potency dual-target therapeutic peptides with ORIDTP

De novo design of high-potency dual-target therapeutic peptides with ORIDTP

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 21 min read (4136 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~21 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Peptides capable of modulating two therapeutic targets offer opportunities for treating complex diseases1,2.
  • This is a preview of subscription content, access via your institution.
  • Access Nature and 54 other Nature Portfolio journals.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Peptides capable of modulating two therapeutic targets offer opportunities for treating complex diseases1,2. However, the development of such peptides at both targets is challenging, limited primarily by low design success rates and weak bioactivity. Here we present ORIDTP, an artificial intelligence platform that integrates single-target knowledge transfer and dual-target reinforcement to enable the rational design of high-potency peptides. ORIDTP successfully designed dual-target co-agonists for the GLP-1R and glucagon receptor (GCGR, also known as GLR), six of which surpassed the strongest natural binders of each receptor in bioactivity. Notably, the lead peptide GA-Dual.R5.S3 induced substantial weight loss and glycaemic improvement in diet-induced obese mice, and exhibited pronounced antidiabetic effects in db/db mice, without inducing nausea or aversion. Furthermore, ORIDTP demonstrated generalizability through successful zero-shot design of dual-target co-inhibitors for structurally and mechanistically distinct immune checkpoints, PD-1 and CTLA-4. Out of 15 designed peptides, 8 blocked both checkpoint interactions and 3 further exhibited in vivo antitumour efficacy in human checkpoint knock-in tumour-bearing mice. The lead peptide IC-Dual.P3 achieved the strongest tumour growth suppression, reducing tumour volume by 94.2% relative to controls. Together, these findings establish ORIDTP as a powerful and generalizable platform for de novo dual-target peptide discovery.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Carter White | 26 Nov 2026 13:09, Last updated: 27 Nov 2026 11:54.

Looking to gain ground in the race for automatic promotion, West Bromwich Albion welcome Bristol City to The Hawthorns for a Championship contest on Saturday afternoon.

The Baggies are in the midst of an impressive unbeaten run in the second tier, making them the favourites with the best UK betting apps 2026 to record victory over the out-of-form Robins.

Since a 1-0 defeat by Birmingham City at The Hawthorns on October 10, West Brom have strung together an eight-game unbeaten streak (W5 D3) in the Championship, beating Bolton Wanderers last time out.

Wednesday night's match at the Toughsheet Community Stadium provided the stage for Albion's Norwegian stars to shine, with Aune Heggebo (2) and Felix Horn Myhre scoring in a 3-1 success over the Wanderers.

Now boasting the best away record in the division with 17 points collected from nine outings, James Morrison's side are back at The Hawthorns this weekend, when they will be striving for a repeat of their 3-0 battering of Millwall in the Black Country prior to the international break.

One of four Midlands clubs inside the top five of the Championship standings after 17 matches, West Brom are occupying fifth spot in the table, just three points behind pacesetters Middlesbrough and Stoke City.

Scoring an eye-catching eight goals across their past three league fixtures, the Baggies pose danger from an array of positions, with five different players scoring three or more Championship goals so far this term.

Following three consecutive losses at the beginning of their tricky November schedule, Bristol City stopped the rot with a respectable 1-1 draw with Wrexham at Ashton Gate on Tuesday night.

It looked as if the Robins were hurtling towards their ninth defeat of the league campaign when Joe Worrall opened the scoring early on, but Cameron Pring's first goal in nearly three years secured a share of the spoils.

Winning just one of his past nine second-tier contests (D3 L5) in charge, Michael Skubala remains under severe pressure at Bristol City, who currently reside in an uninspiring 16th place in the table.

The Robins' sole victory in their current wretched run arrived on the road at Bolton on October 31, when Dom Ballard, Sam Bell and playmaker Scott Twine netted in a five-goal thriller.

Firing an attacking blank in five of their past eight matches ahead of Saturday's trip to The Hawthorns, there is no doubting that the Robins are failing to maximise the potential of Ballard and Lorent Tolaj, with the pair scoring 40 goals combined in League One last term.

West Bromwich Albion Championship form:.

Bristol City Championship form:.

After leading goalscorer Isaac Price missed the win at Bolton on Wednesday, West Brom boss Morrison revealed that the Northern Irishman is set to be sidelined for up to six weeks due to a knee injury.

The attacker joins midfielder Ousmane Diakite (calf) in the Albion treatment room, with the Mali international expected to be out until late December.

Right-back Noah Galves (knee) will not play again this season, whilst talented youngster Rabby Nzingoula is suspended for this weekend after collecting his fifth yellow card of the term at Bolton.

There was a serious injury scare for Bristol City on Tuesday night, when centre-back Luke McNally was forced off due to a knee issue.

The 27-year-old has previously missed nearly two years due to a problem with the same knee, meaning that Rob Dickie is likely to be drafted into the XI at The Hawthorns.

Sam Greenwood and Lisav Eissat were surprise omissions from the matchday squad last time out but could return to the fold on Saturday.

West Bromwich Albion possible starting lineup:.

O'Leary; Pereira, Mepham, Campbell, Styles; Tunde, Horn Myhre, Molumby, Whitwell; Morgan, Heggebo.

Bristol City possible starting lineup:.

Collins; Tanner, Dickie, Atkinson, Pring; Wallace, Knight, Randell, Twine; Tolaj, Ballard.

Aiming to extend their unbeaten run to nine matches, West Brom will be confident of beating Bristol City, even with Nzingoula, Price and Diakite all sidelined.

The Robins are certainly capable of producing a gutsy away performance but are likely to leave empty-handed on Saturday.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

There will be many more Champions League nights for Rio Ngumoha, although the 18-year-old will always remember this career landmark when his teenage skill plunged the opposition into fearful indecision and decided the game.

This young man has not yet played 40 senior games but there is no doubting the quality. Alexis Mac Allister scored twice, Liverpool came from two goals behind, and it all ended with a panic that meant they came close to chucking it away again. But what everyone could agree on from this strange match of fluctuating fortunes was that Ngumoha looks like one of the best young players in Europe. He is also a bona fide two-sided winger, winning this game for Liverpool from the right wing rather than his conventional left-wing role.

It has been revealed that ngumoha created the second Liverpool goal for Ronald Araújo and then the third for Mac Allister with the game’s best moment. That was an electrifying run into a group of converging yellow shirts in which he beat two men and still retained the composure to pick out Mac Allister in the area. Even as the Argentine ran to the Kop to celebrate, that stand was chanting the name of the teenager from east London. Ngumoha was one of three academy boys in Andoni Iraola’s XI, along with Lewis Koumas and Trey Nyoni, and all had an impact.

Magic from Rio Ngumoha 🤩🪄 Alexis Mac Allister puts Liverpool ahead with his second goal of the night ⚽️ https://t.co/3FTNWOUYhl.

In a recent development, iraola noted later that Ngumoha had taken care of the defensive work too against Sergi Cardona, an attacking left-back who scored his team’s second goal. From an attacking point of view, Iraola agreed, Ngumoha had periods of the game when he looked unstoppable. “If we can put Rio in situations one-v-one, he makes plays, [and] he produces things,” Iraola noted. “The assist for Alexis is a lovely play. He could go down for a penalty but he decides to continue which is a great decision. Also endurance-wise he is able to play more minutes.”.

He becomes the youngest Liverpool player in Champions League history to register an assist in the competition. For Iraola it will be hard to leave Ngumoha out of the game against in-form Brighton and Hove Albion on Sunday. “I believe in myself to do it,” Ngumoha said to Amazon Prime TV. “The more chances we get, the more it makes the opposition worry. I just keep going and be ruthless.”.

It has been revealed that iraola would later bring on the three £100m attackers whom he had left on the bench, with Sunday’s game in mind. Florian Wirtz, a half-time arrival, scored the fourth and Bradley Barcola and Alexander Isak would later come on. Hard to call how it might go at home to Brighton. Liverpool’s defending was erratic at times, but their comeback was impressive.

The floodgates are opening ⚽️ Florian Wirtz scores his first goal of the season for Liverpool 🇩🇪 https://t.co/5HP72tA3bE.

In a recent development, iraola made major changes at half-time, substituting Araújo and playing without a conventional right-back for the second half. It was brave and changed the momentum of the game, pushing his team higher up the pitch in what looked like a man-to-man marking arrangement. It enabled Iraola’s players to deny Villarreal the space and possession they had enjoyed in the first half when they had taken a two-goal lead – chiefly because of the mistakes of the home team. However much that was destabilising for Liverpool, by half-time they were level.

Recent findings suggest that “They are so good on the ball,” Iraola said of Villarreal afterwards. Indeed, Villarreal’s manager Iñigo Pérez, a former Athletic team-mate of the Liverpool manager, was a coach whom Iraola sought to appoint at Bournemouth. “People probably don’t rate them [Villarreal],” Iraola said, “but after Barça they are probably the best in La Liga. They have 61 per cent of possession. Probably they have not had the results they deserve. If you are not really aggressive, you are not going to get the ball.

“We didn’t take as much risk. We were struggling because it is not a team that you can just press a bit. Either you go all the way or you will struggle without the ball.” Once Liverpool had done so, he said, his team had “won a lot of duels”. He was right in that respect. With the space squeezed, it was the power of Liverpool’s midfield that was telling.

It has been revealed that virgil van Dijk gave the first goal to Villarreal’s small No 9 Georges Mikautadze who had looked up to that point like he was hopelessly mismatched against the Liverpool captain and Jérémy Jacquet. Van Dijk’s misjudged header back to Alisson let in the striker, who did well to gather the ball and then hit it early. The second Villarreal goal at the midpoint of the first half was a mistake from Kostas Tsimikas, who failed to step up and played both Mikautadze and Cardona onside from Nathan Saliba’s ball. Either might have tucked it in but it was the left-back Cardona who took it on.

A moment to forget for Virgil van Dijk 😨 Georges Mikautadze takes full advantage to give Villarreal the lead at Anfield 🟡⚽️ https://t.co/3JTl00UwYa.

The pace of the game was slow and Villarreal were in control until the later stages of the half. Koumas and Cody Gakpo created a chance and from the corner that resulted Mac Allister headed in Tsimikas’s cross. Liverpool were up and running. Ngumoha’s cross from the left was unwisely left by Cardona for Araújo to score and the game was level.

Out of nowhere 😳 Ronald Araújo sneaks in to grab Liverpool's equaliser on the stroke of half-time 🇺🇾 https://t.co/Qrn8PmB2bJ.

Then came Ngumoha’s substantial second half, creating the third for Mac Allister. The teenager went past Cardona and the substitute Juan Foyth in a couple of strides. Wirtz dispatched the fourth from Gakpo’s ball.

Recent findings suggest that even so there was still time for Liverpool to show that they had sacrificed some defensive stability. The absence of a right-back cost them when substitute Tani Oluwaseyi ran into that area of the pitch to score Villarreal’s third late on. The third win of Liverpool’s Champions League season puts them second in the 36-team super-table, and behind defending champions Paris St-Germain only on goal difference.

It has been revealed that liverpool are also seeing a newly introduced star emerge. Ngumoha might be the most expensive academy signing in the game’s modern history but alongside the £100m men he looks like a risk that was worth taking.

We have stated all night about momentum, and talking about how they Liverpool will play against Brighton at the weekend, I’ll be amazed if Rio [Ngumoha] doesn’t start because of the momentum that he has got from this game.

You see the fans, you see how everyone got a lift by him and that’s what they need at the weekend, they need someone to lift them.

Recent findings suggest that they are flying. Their confidence is through the roof. A similar style to Villarreal. They are second in everything after Barcelona. It has been a good game to prepare and we will use it.

It has been revealed that I am really happy with Rio. He is trying to improve everything and we are trying to correct things. He played a lot on the left and know he is playing a lot on the right and he has adapted really well. We encourage him always. Even defensively as well he is improving. He has become a more complete player – and we must not forget he is 18!

Recent findings suggest that rio Ngumoha was magnificent tonight. Such a threat, and he dedicated himself to his tasks. On the ball this kid has so much potential, and I say kid, but he’s a young man. He has so much quality and it’s stuff that you can’t teach to be honest.

It has been revealed that what he does with the ball at his feet, that is God given ability, and his hard work on the training pitch, doing things day in and day out, and being ruthless, is what he remarked in his interview, and I like that. He wants to be decisive, and I love that about him.

I’m not tall but I love going in the box. I really like it. They know I like to attack the near post. I scored in the World Cup as well. It was a good header. The second goal, Rio, was amazing. I talk with him about cutting it back on the floor.

Industry observers note that it’s not something I really practice. My dad is a bit smaller than me but he was quite good in the air so maybe it’s something I got from him.

Last year was a really difficult year for all of us. It was clear I was not at the level and I am the first one to say. Something wasn’t right in the group and this manager changed it. The way we play is different, I don’t like to compare. I’m feeling good.

Recent findings suggest that A lot of things happened today. They were much better than us in the first half and we were much better in the second half. When we’ve been under pressure, we answered well. When we relaxed, we made mistakes. You cannot relax against very good opposition. I value the win.

We have to know that if we don’t go to the limit, it will be difficult. We are facing very good teams. It’s good to come back but we’ve started losing too many goals this season.

Florian Wirtz has scored or assisted in three consecutive games for the first time in his Liverpool career: 🅰️ vs LASK 🅰️ vs Brentford ⚽️ vs Villarreal https://t.co/woLWk2SGGL.

In a recent development, it was a top performance from the boys. We were two goals down but the mentality was always there. We knew we were going to win.

It’s up there with one of the best I’ve played. I enjoyed myself and the team helped me a lot.

It has been revealed that whenever I get the ball and there’s an opportunity to go one v one or two v one, I believe in myself. I’ll just keep going and be ruthless.

In a recent development, rio Ngumoha talking to Gabriel Clarke on Amazon Prime: “Definitely one of the best games I played. I enjoyed it. Whenever I get the ball and go one v one, the more it makes the opposition worried.”.

When he was reminded that he was the youngest Englishman to provide an assist in the Champions League, he noted: “Records are amazing to break.”.

It has been revealed that and on playing on the right instead of the left wing: “It’s helped me a lot in training. Slowly I’m getting better on the right.”.

And to hear the crowd chanting his name: “This stadium, we have the best fans. To hear my name being chanted is a dream.”.

In a recent development, PSG’s 4-2 win over Barcelona tonight also puts them on nine points. Aston Villa, Arsenal, Real Madrid, Sporting and Real Betis are the teams playing tomorrow night with the opportunity to maintain a 100 per cent record.

It has been revealed that nine points from a possible nine for Liverpool in the Champions League, but they made hard work of it. Some dysfunction was probably to be expected after Iraola decided to start without Mac Allister, Isak, Wirtz and Barcola, but their defensive structure was unzipped far too easily at times.

On the other hand, they dragged themselves off the canvas and the night belonged to Rio Ngumoha. He looked dangerous every time he received the ball, set up the third goal, and received a standing ovation when he was substituted. Liverpool need to put that contract in front of him sharpish.

Still time for another hairy moment at the back for Liverpool, but Perez’ shot from the edge of the area is blocked and that will surely be that.

It has been revealed that pape Gueye floats a cross straight down the throat of Alisson. A wasted opportunity for Villarreal. But still a couple of minutes to play.

Just the three minutes of added time to play, and Liverpool are probably grateful for that.

It has been revealed that could Liverpool be in for a nervous finish? Their defence is caught square again after a run in behind from Ayoze Perez, and Oluwaseyi was totally unmarked at the back post to apply a simple finish at silence Anfield.

Cody Gakpo threatens to score Liverpool’s fifth with an overhead free-kick, teed up by McConnell’s chipped cross to the back post, but he could not keep the attempt down.

The game is meandering towards its conclusion now, though a Villarreal goal would make things interesting.

Another Liverpool youngster enjoys a taste of first-team actions: James McConnell is on for Nyoni.

Alexis Mac Allister’s second goal but Anfield also singing about Rio Ngumoha. He went past two Villarreal defenders to create that one. He has been outstanding.

Recent findings suggest that there will be time to talk more about Rio Ngumoha – this is his best performance in a Liverpool shirt, a coming-of-age night if you will – but it cannot be overlooked how Alexis Mac Allister has been transformed. He was unrecognisable last season but now he is every inch the man who was a major cog in the push for the title.

Nyoni’s standing foot was slipping, but he made a clean connection on his shot from range and it whistled just wide of the foot of the post. Ngumoha then has the crowd cooing again, with another drop of the shoulder to beat his man.

In a recent development, gravenberch found himself sweeping up as Liverpool’s last man, there. The second half has had a more conventional feel, Liverpool making the running as they shoot towards the Kop and their opponents soaking up the pressure. A game of fewer chances since the break.

Always helps having knowledge in close vicinity: a quick discussion with Rafa Benitez about Liverpool’s set up for the second period. Polo shirt and slacks for the young Spanish coach.

Subs: Junior, Costa, Freeman, Diatta, Gerard, Foyth, Akhomach, Macia, Oluwaseyi, Perez, El Jmili, Gaitan Diaz.

Liverpool XI: Alisson; Araujo, Jacquet, Van Dijk, Tsimikas; Gravenberch, Nyoni, Mac Allister; Ngumoha, Koumas, Gakpo.

Subs: Mamardashvili, Woodman, Gomez, Kerkez, Wirtz, Isak, Barcola, Chambers, McConnell, Danns, Laffey.

A very interesting team selection from Andoni Iraola. Liverpool’s head coach had indicated at his pre-match press conference that he was going to go as strong as possible, as his side seek to secure their third straight Champions League win. But the very fact Iraola has chosen to put Florian Wirtz and Bradley Barcola on the bench indicates he has one eye on Sunday’s demanding assignment against Brighton at Anfield.

Iraola will be delighted to have Cody Gakpo fit again and Lewis Koumas certainly deserves another opportunity to lead the line. But after victory’s against Atletico Madrid and LASK, Liverpool have given themselves some breathing space and it is understandable if Iraola, who has bemoaned the lack of time he has to train his squad, is already plotting Brighton’s downfall.

Recent findings suggest that your Reds to take on Villarreal in the #UCL! 🔴💫 https://t.co/tlQNFZVMBv.

Sources indicate that the club known as the “Yellow Submarine” made themselves some fans in the red half of Merseyside by denying Everton a place in the Champions League proper in 2005/06. Everton lost 4-2 on aggregate, and there was controversy in the second leg in Spain when Pierluigi Collina disallowed a Duncan Ferguson header that could have taken the tie to extra time. Everton had finished fourth, one place above Liverpool, the previous season, but Liverpool’s triumph in Istanbul assured them of a qualification place too. Unlike Everton, they prevailed.

Speaking of which, Rafael Benitez is at Anfield this evening.

Recent findings suggest that dominic King takes stock of Andoni Iraola’s first 10 games in charge of Liverpool and, despite some teething problems, he believes there are reasons to be optimistic. The demands Iraola is putting on Liverpool’s midfielders are an interesting tactical wrinkle, with Dom writing: “Liverpool’s formation will always be written as 4-2-3-1, but the reality is that Iraola’s team do not play in four clear tactical lines. He asks specific jobs of his midfielders, deploying them detailed instructions, and it is going to require some patience before performances become consistent.”.

A precious victory at Brentford, Bradley Barcola and Alexander Isak among the goals and a couple of improved showings from Florian Wirtz mean things now look a little brighter for Liverpool.

They are strong favourites to make it nine points from nine in the Champions League by beating Villarreal at Anfield this evening, the Spanish club they vanquished in the 2022 semi-finals under Jürgen Klopp.

Sources indicate that liverpool drew Atletico Madrid at home (already ticked off) and Inter Milan away as their two pot-one fixtures, which is about as kind as you can expect. A top-two finish in the league phase is a realistic aspiration for Andoni Iraola’s team, and something would need to go badly awry for them to miss out on the top eight.

Cody Gakpo, Dominik Szoboszlai and Isak returned from injury to strengthen Liverpool at Brentford, although Szoboszlai has been lost for a few weeks following another hamstring complication.

Villarreal have punched well above their weight in Europe for the past few decades, reaching two European Cup semi-finals (beaten by Arsenal in 2006 as well as Liverpool in 2022) and winning the Europa League under Unai Emery in 2021.

They have been mediocre in La Liga so far this season though, 12th after nine games on nine points and with a goal difference of zero. Their Champions League performances have been promising though, losing by the odd goal in a frantic finish at Borussia Dortmund and beating Napoli 3-1 at home. Villarreal’s best player is probably Senegalese central midfielder Pape Gueye, and former Arsenal winger Nicolas Pépé is also in their ranks. Gueye, despite his position, is their joint-top scorer in all competitions with three goals.

Iraola will be up against his close friend and former Athletic Bilbao team-mate Inigo Perez who is now in charge at Villarreal. Perez was also Iraola’s assistant at Rayo Vallecano, the job which earned the Basque his move to Bournemouth. Perez guided Rayo Vallecano to the Uefa Conference League final last season.

Latest Update: Erling Haaland sparks fear among fans after concerning TV interview as he admits he is 'questioning everything' after Man City's draw with Napoli

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 04:06 EST, 25 November 2026 | Updated: 08:33 EST, 25 November 2026.
  • Manchester City fans have expressed concern over Erling Haaland's despondent interview following their Champions League draw with Napoli, with the star admitting he is 'questioning everything' amid their slump in form.
  • Enzo Maresca's side rescued a late draw at the Etihad on Tuesday night, with Rayan Cherki equalising in the 86th minute to secure a 2-2 draw with Napoli.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By MICHAEL PAVITT, SPORTS REPORTER.

Published: 04:06 EST, 25 November 2026 | Updated: 08:33 EST, 25 November 2026.

Manchester City fans have expressed concern over Erling Haaland's despondent interview following their Champions League draw with Napoli, with the star admitting he is 'questioning everything' amid their slump in form.

Enzo Maresca's side rescued a late draw at the Etihad on Tuesday night, with Rayan Cherki equalising in the 86th minute to secure a 2-2 draw with Napoli.

The result, however, continued an underwhelming run of form with Man City having won just twice in their last seven matches – one of which was achieved in a penalty shoot-out against Brighton in the Carabao Cup.

Man City have suffered defeats to Aston Villa, Brighton and Nottingham Forest in the Premier League in the run, as well as drawing with Fulham on the weekend.

Haaland, who captained Man City against Napoli, admitted post-match to TNT Sports that their underwhelming form has left the squad questioning themselves.

'We were not able to control and attack the game in the way we want,' Haaland noted. 'Football is easy and difficult. When you win it's easy and you know what to do. When you don't you start questioning everything.

Erling Haaland cut a despondent figure as he admitted to 'questioning everything' after Man City's draw with Napoli continued their underwhelming form.

Industry observers note that 🗣️ "I have no idea what we were missing. You could feel it in the last few games that there's something that's not clicking fully."@Erling reflects on @ManCity's 2-2 draw with Napoli.🎤 @AndyKerrtv #UCL | #ManCity pic.twitter.com/Cx2Hzieom3.

'The perfect thing would be to not think but it's not so easy.

Sources indicate that 'We have so much quality so it's about getting the quality out in every player. We have to regroup, stay positive and bring energy on the pitch and try to do our best.'.

Haaland admitted in another interview with Bein Sports that the run of form 'hurts', with the star having offered a resigned laugh when asked whether the draw against Napoli should be considered a 'good point'.

The 26-year-old was seen looking down throughout the minute and a half interview, while he also rubbed his face with his hand as he looked to find answers for Man City's recent struggles.

'How the game was we managed to come back two times, but we demand more,' Haaland said.

'We have to do better and find some ways to control the game more and perform in a better way.

Recent findings suggest that 'I have no idea what we were missing. You could feel it in the last few games that it is not clicking fully and we have to find out, stay positive and get the best out of every single day.

'With and without the armband I feel huge responsibility because all I want to do is perform for this club and win games for Man City and right now we are not doing that. It hurts.'.

Fans quickly noted Haaland's downbeat responses to questions and despondent body language during the interview.

Man City fans have expressed concerns over Haaland's downbeat responses and body language in the interview.

Fans claimed they have never seen Haaland 'looking this flat' and suggested the star 'looks distraught' amid their underwhelming run.

'I've never seen Haaland looking this flat. Not even close to it,' one commented.

It has been revealed that 'At least he’s being honest with himself. Looks distraught,' a second stated, with a third writing 'Extremely concerning.'.

'Never seen Erling Haaland look like this before,' another added, while a Man City fan wrote 'You can really tell how confused Haaland is from his expression. They don’t have confidence in their own football.'.

One went as far as claiming 'Haaland looks like he’s done with Manchester City…' while sharing footage of his reaction to one of Napoli's goals on the night.

Other fans questioned whether Haaland and his Man City team-mates' recent slump may be related to concerns over the potential punishment the club could face for breaching financial rules.

Man City were found guilty of the vast majority of charges brought against them by the Premier League for financial wrongdoing when the verdict was released in September. The club have since appealed.

An independent commission ruled Man City had disguised payments worth £900million in a nine-year period with ‘sham’ deals.

Man City were found to have artificially inflated sponsorship agreements and pumped money into the club from its Abu Dhabi owners via disguised payments in a bid to swerve Premier League spending rules.

Man City have continued to insist they had 'irrefutable evidence' proving their innocence, but if the club loses its appeal, the Premier League have a range of sanctions at their disposal – including relegation or expulsion.

Man City face Arsenal in a crucial match on Sunday as they look to make inroads in the Gunners six point lead at the top of the Premier League.

Haaland had pushed back against suggestions the case had affected their form during the international break, while stressing he was committed long-term to the club.

The forward's first answer to Norwegian broadcaster TV2 had spanned two minutes and 14 seconds, as he reeled off the teams he had represented from 2009 to 2018, the years covered by the charges after he was asked about the club's situation.

'In 2009, I played for Bryne U9s. In 2010, the U10s. In 2011, the U11s. 2012, the U12s, 2013, the U13s. Shall we continue? We don't need the whole list. 2014, the U14s. 2015, the U15s and the national team,' Haaland remarked.

Recent findings suggest that 'Then the U16s, I think. In 2016, I moved up to Bryne's first team, second team and youth team. In 2017, I went to Molde. In 2018, I was with Molde. The first team, Molde 2 and a bit with the youth team.

'So this is a question I struggle to answer because it's a legal battle….

'It's a case between the Premier League and Manchester City that a panel will deal with. Am I supposed to answer that? I'm not really sure.'.

He continued: 'It's a difficult question to answer when I don't really know that much about it.

It has been revealed that 'I assume the answers will come… I don't know when. I haven't read much about it.

'To be completely honest, I'm focused on trying to perform for Manchester City.

The Man City star, who signed a nine-and-a-half-year contract in late 2024, told Norwegian television earlier this month that his focus was on helping the team to turn their form around.

The draw against Napoli leaves Man City lying sixth in the Champions League table - which would be enough to see Maresca's side to qualify for the last-16.

Man City face a crucial clash on the weekend when they face reigning champions Arsenal in the Premier League, as they look to halve the six-point gap to the leaders at the top of the table.

Latest Update: Le Havre vs. Strasbourg - prediction, team news, lineups

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (592 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Seye Omidiora | 26 Nov 2026 13:09.
  • Two of Ligue 1's struggling sides meet in Saturday's gameweek 12 encounter, as winless Le Havre host third-bottom Strasbourg at Stade Oceane.
  • The bottom club remain the only side without a victory in the French top flight after 11 matches, leaving their survival prospects looking increasingly bleak even at this stage of the campaign.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Seye Omidiora | 26 Nov 2026 13:09.

Two of Ligue 1's struggling sides meet in Saturday's gameweek 12 encounter, as winless Le Havre host third-bottom Strasbourg at Stade Oceane.

The bottom club remain the only side without a victory in the French top flight after 11 matches, leaving their survival prospects looking increasingly bleak even at this stage of the campaign.

Le Havre's 14th-placed finish last season, just three points above Nice in the relegation playoff spot, offered little encouragement ahead of the 2026-27 campaign, and those concerns have proved justified.

Le Club Doyen have not won a top-flight fixture since beating Lorient 2-0 on the final day of last season, with their miserable start prompting Didier Digard's dismissal at the end of October.

Valerien Ismael's first match in charge of the basement club began brightly when Josh Maja scored after three minutes against Troyes; however, they held that advantage for just 15 minutes before eventually losing 3-1.

Conceding three more goals left Les Ciel et Marine with the competition's joint-worst defensive record, having shipped 25, while their tally of 10 scored surpasses only Angers' nine.

Even victory would do little to transform the Dean Club's position, as they enter this weekend eight points behind the relegation playoff spot and nine adrift of safety.

Nonetheless, the hosts must avoid defeat to Vitor Matos's Strasbourg, who occupy that playoff position.

Le Racing's disappointing start has already cost Hugo Oliveira his job, with Matos replacing his Portuguese compatriot during the international break.

The latest manager's debut did not go to plan, with Le RCS losing 1-0 to Brest despite an encouraging performance in which they attempted 15 shots to their opponents' 16; Le Racing also created two chances deemed clear-cut to Brest's one.

Looking to build on that display, Le RCS target their fourth victory of the campaign this weekend, although it would be only their second since early October.

Maximum points could lift Matos's men out of the playoff spot and as high as 13th, although escaping the bottom three also requires Auxerre, Troyes or Le Mans to slip up.

The hosts have several absentees, with Felix Mambimbi (Achilles), Timothee Pembele (muscle), Rassoul Ndiaye (muscle), Daren Mosengo (ankle), Stephan Zagadou (ACL), Sota Nakamura (leg) and Lionel Mpasi (Achilles) all sidelined.

Enzo Koffi begins a two-match suspension following his late dismissal against Troyes last weekend, ruling him out of Saturday's encounter and December's trip to Lens.

Only six players have surpassed Maja's five league goals this season, but the Nigerian's efforts have brought little reward for a Dean Club side repeatedly undermined by defensive frailties.

Strasbourg have several potential game-changers, with Gessime Yassine registering four goals and three assists, Giovanni Reyna scoring three, Conrad Harder and Dario Essugo contributing two goals and an assist and Sebastian Nanasi setting up three.

However, Reyna is unavailable due to a muscle problem, while Fabio Balde (leg), Oso (knock) and Joaquin Panichelli (ACL) are also sidelined.

Le Havre possible starting lineup:.

Bodart; Sasso, Seko, Touba; Ouziad, Mwanga, Ebonog, Richardson, Jelert; Maja, Fofana.

Strasbourg possible starting lineup:.

Jorgensen; Antwi, Doukoure, Coulibaly, Hogsberg; Essugo, El Mourabet; Yassine, Nanasi, Godo; Harder.

Maja's scoring form offers Le Havre some encouragement, but conceding 25 goals in 11 matches suggests that their defensive problems remain too pronounced for an immediate recovery.

Strasbourg created enough chances to trouble Brest in Matos's first match and should find greater reward against the division's joint-leakiest defence.

Tesla to 'wind down' production of flop Cybertruck

📅 06 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (676 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Tesla owner Elon Musk said on Friday that the firm would scale down production of the Cybertruck at its Austin factory in the coming year.
  • The South African entrepreneur noted Tesla would be scaling back production of his futuristic but often-mocked pickup truck and amping up production of what he hopes will soon become a fleet of fully automated taxis.
  • "Tesla will be winding down production of the cybertruck at Gigafactory Texas around the middle of next year to make room for increased Cybercab production," Musk said on his X social media site.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Tesla owner Elon Musk said on Friday that the firm would scale down production of the Cybertruck at its Austin factory in the coming year.

The South African entrepreneur noted Tesla would be scaling back production of his futuristic but often-mocked pickup truck and amping up production of what he hopes will soon become a fleet of fully automated taxis.

"Tesla will be winding down production of the cybertruck at Gigafactory Texas around the middle of next year to make room for increased Cybercab production," Musk said on his X social media site.

The announcement follows a bruising week for Musk amid the US midterm elections, where Republicans struggled despite his major donations, with his companies losing billions in value by market capitalization as investors sought to ditch stock.

Musk later responded to a complimentary user online who hailed the Cybertruck as the "best vehicle Tesla has ever made," and calling it an "end of an era" by saying: "True.".

For years he had poured much of his enthusiastic marketing zeal into promoting the Cybertruck, saying during the 2023 launch "finally, the future will look like the future.".

However the oversized body, straight lines and stainless steel and the post-apocalpytic vibe these created also met with widespread criticism and even mockery.

The electric powertrain was probably a barrier to sales in the US, by far the biggest pickup truck market, where Musk had hoped to take on some of the country's top-selling gas-guzzling vehicles like the Ford F150 or the Chevrolet Silverado and the Dodge Ram.

Meanwhile, the car's striking shape, weight and size made it impossible for Tesla to try to crack Europe, where electric vehicles are gaining a much larger market share.

Industry observers note that unlike in the US, EU safety regulations place considerable emphasis not just on people in cars in accidents, but also on the dangers posed to pedestrians who might be hit by a vehicle. That meant it was not possible for Tesla to register and sell the Cybertruck for road use in Europe.

Beyond this, the vehicle's size would likely have rendered it impractical and unpopular on many European roads, where space tends to be at more of a premium.

Depending how quick the wind-down proves to be, the Cybertruck's production run could prove shorter than its five-year R&D phase.

Given its longstanding problems meeting Musk's very public sales and production predictions, Tesla does not publish sales figures broken down by model.

But according to the automotive data platform Kelley Blue Book, the company sold 20,237 Cybertrucks in the US last year, down from 38,965 in 2024.

At launch in 2023, Musk had predicted unit sales nearer a quarter of a million.

Sources indicate that for orientation, Ford sold more than 800,000 F-Series pickups in the US last year, a slight boost on 2024's numbers. These vehicles start at less than half the list price of a Cybertruck in the US.

The IPO for SpaceX this year revealed that Musk's second-largest manufacturer was comfortably the biggest buyer of Cybertrucks in 2025. It bought vehicles worth $131 million and did not even enjoy a bulk-buy or friends-rate discount, paying list prices for the fleet.

The Cybercab is a vehicular element in Musk's bid to transform Tesla towards a tech giant focused more on AI and robotics than automobilies.

Rather than just featuring the self-drive or driving assistance programs that Musk has been championing for years, the Cybercab has no steering wheels, pedals or mirrors at all and is designed never to have a human in control.

Musk say the model will be the company's main autonomous model and will supply a global network of Robotaxis.

Starting in the past few months, around 300 such vehicles have been registered and have started operating, on approved roads in the Austin area near Tesla's Gigafactory Texas. They're being added to the existing fleet of autonomous Model Y Teslas being used for the purpose, serving in an area known as a geofence of around 680 square kilometers (264 square miles).

  • Arsenal could face an unexpected transfer decision in January, with Kepa Arrizabalaga's future at the Emirates Stadium uncertain.
  • The Spanish goalkeeper is understood to be unhappy with his current situation and is not ruling out a mid-season departure.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Lewis Blain | 26 Nov 2026 13:11.

Arsenal could face an unexpected transfer decision in January, with Kepa Arrizabalaga's future at the Emirates Stadium uncertain.

The Spanish goalkeeper is understood to be unhappy with his current situation and is not ruling out a mid-season departure.

A potential exit would leave Gunners boss Mikel Arteta needing to consider an additional goalkeeper, despite other areas of his squad appearing to require greater attention.

Kepa joined Arsenal from Chelsea in July 2025 and spent the past 18 months as David Raya's deputy, making 12 appearances in all competitions, including just one in the Premier League.

He has started only twice this season, with his latest appearance coming in Tuesday's 1-1 draw against Borussia Dortmund in the Champions League, when Raya was unavailable through injury.

Reports in Spain (via Sport Witness) have linked the 32-year-old with Valencia, with sporting director Braulio Vazquez reportedly exploring the possibility of bringing him back to LaLiga.

It is understood that there is nothing concrete at this stage, with Kepa yet to receive a formal approach or offer from the Spanish club.

The shot-stopper has also not held talks with Arsenal over his future, although the possibility of him initiating discussions with the club's hierarchy has not been ruled out.

Kepa's contract at the Emirates runs until 2028, but his future remains uncertain, with Valencia potentially revisiting their interest in the January window.

Arsenal have obvious priorities elsewhere, particularly in attack, where additional options on the wing and at centre-forward could strengthen Arteta's squad as they look to defend their Premier League crown.

However, allowing Kepa to leave in January, even on loan, would create an unexpected problem between the posts.

With Raya, Kepa and Illan Meslier presently providing the goalkeeping options, losing the Spaniard would leave the Gunners needing to consider another addition to maintain sufficient cover.

The club would surely prefer to avoid that situation until the summer, and that makes sense given the other areas that could demand investment.

Unless Kepa pushes for an exit or Valencia make an offer that Arsenal are willing to consider, keeping him until the end of the season would appear the simplest solution.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • According to recent reports, the significant three bring a lot of attention to Italy and their footballing ecosystem, but that’s not all.
  • As Gazzetta dello Sport writes, via Calciomercato.com, Inter recorded the highest revenue last season of €518 million, Juventus slotted in with €474.4m and then the Rossoneri finished ‘last’ with a revenue of €464.6m.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Last night, a report was published comparing the financials of AC Milan, Juventus and Inter and the findings are very interesting.

According to recent reports, the significant three bring a lot of attention to Italy and their footballing ecosystem, but that’s not all. Indeed, all three bring in vast amounts of money and have done so for years, which has helped them establish this dominance. However, their records last season show that a change could be on the way.

As Gazzetta dello Sport writes, via Calciomercato.com, Inter recorded the highest revenue last season of €518 million, Juventus slotted in with €474.4m and then the Rossoneri finished ‘last’ with a revenue of €464.6m.

However, the profits – about that – of all three clubs didn’t line up in the same order. Inter recorded a €23m loss, then it was Milan with a €24m loss – largely helped by the summer signings – and Juventus finished last with a €66m loss.

In a recent development, considering the Nerazzurri’s sporting successes in recent years, it makes sense why revenues are considerably higher, especially when looking at their Champions League records. For example, not being in Europe cost the Diavolo €54m between 2024/25 and 2025/26.

According to recent reports, in terms of squad cost, the Biaconeri were uncontested at the top, with a wage of €210m per season. Inter finished just below with €204m per season, whilst the Rossoneri ‘only’ spent €146m. Of course, this is still lucrative.

All in all, the foundations laid at Casa Milan are looking strong and if they can become more successful, their revenues could rocket up.

  • Liverpool are back in action on Sunday afternoon when they square off against Everton in the Merseyside derby.
  • Andoni Iraola's side start the next batch of fixtures sitting in fourth position in the Premier League table.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Darren Plant | 26 Nov 2026 13:18, Last updated: 27 Nov 2026 10:45.

Liverpool are back in action on Sunday afternoon when they square off against Everton in the Merseyside derby.

Andoni Iraola's side start the next batch of fixtures sitting in fourth position in the Premier League table.

However, although they earned an impressive 3-0 win at Club Brugge in the Champions League in midweek, the Spaniard is dealing with a number of injury concerns.

Here, Sports Mole rounds up Liverpool’s latest injury and suspension news ahead of their showdown with Everton, who are still reeling from their 4-0 defeat at Brentford last time out.

Possible return date: December 2 (vs. Sunderland).

Cody Gakpo was a surprise absentee from the Liverpool squad against Manchester United, and Iraola subsequently revealed that the attacker had picked up a calf injury on Netherlands duty.

Having also missed the Club Brugge game, the versatile attacker has already been ruled out of this fixture.

Possible return date: November 29 (vs. Everton).

Although Ryan Gravenberch finds himself in a similar position to Gakpo, he has not been conclusively ruled out of this fixture, with Iraola revealing that Liverpool are attempting to 'manage the pain' of his heel issue.

© Imago / Propaganda Photo, David Rawcliffe, Amanda McMaster.

Industry observers note that possible return date: January 2 (vs. Coventry City).

Hugo Ekitike is making continued progress in his rehabilitation from a serious Achilles injury, but the French striker is still expected to miss the rest of 2026.

Iraola suggested prior to the Club Brugge match that January is the current target.

Possible return date: January 2 (vs. Coventry City).

Out for over a year with a serious knee injury, Giovanni Leoni returned to team training during the international break and is now in the "last part" of his recovery process, but a playing comeback before the New Year is still incredibly unlikely.

Iraola has stated that he will have to play in behind-closed-doors or Under-21 fixtures before coming back into contention.

Possible return date: January 2 (vs. Coventry City).

Likewise, Conor Bradley is finally back with his teammates on the training pitches after sustaining a severe knee problem in January, but it will be a few more weeks before he is considered for selection too.

As in the case of Leoni, Bradley will need to come through lower-level matches before being considered for a return.

According to recent reports, possible return date: November 29 (vs. Everton).

Victor Munoz took a heavy knock to his knee against Club Brugge and was subsequently withdrawn. However, after the game, Iraola revealed that the initial pain had subsided, leaving the Spaniard to be assessed ahead of this contest.

Liverpool have no players suspended for this match.

Stevenage vs Blackpool - prediction, team news, lineups

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (898 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Calum Burrowes | 26 Nov 2026 13:22, Last updated: 27 Nov 2026 11:55.
  • Looking to extend their unbeaten run to six matches in all competitions, Stevenage welcome managerless Blackpool to Broadhall Way on Saturday afternoon for the sides' final League One fixture of the month.
  • Boro followed up a 1-0 victory away to Notts County with a goalless draw against Sheffield Wednesday during the week, while the Seasiders claimed their first point under interim boss Steve Thompson thanks to a late Niall Ennis equaliser in an unlikely draw against Leicester City.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Calum Burrowes | 26 Nov 2026 13:22, Last updated: 27 Nov 2026 11:55.

Looking to extend their unbeaten run to six matches in all competitions, Stevenage welcome managerless Blackpool to Broadhall Way on Saturday afternoon for the sides' final League One fixture of the month.

Boro followed up a 1-0 victory away to Notts County with a goalless draw against Sheffield Wednesday during the week, while the Seasiders claimed their first point under interim boss Steve Thompson thanks to a late Niall Ennis equaliser in an unlikely draw against Leicester City.

After suffering playoff heartbreak last season, where Stevenage finished sixth before losing to Stockport County in the semi-finals, the Hertfordshire-based club stuck with Alex Revell in the hope that the former striker could lead Boro one step further this time around.

However, after 14 League One matches, Stevenage sit 13th in the table with five wins, five draws and four defeats leaving them on 20 points, six adrift of the playoff places.

Despite that, they remain closer to the top six than the bottom four and have put together some encouraging results as they look to turn their slow start to the season around.

After beginning the month by securing their place in the next round of the FA Cup, Stevenage finished top of their EFL Trophy group thanks to a penalty shootout victory over Fulham Under-21s, before beating Notts County and drawing with recently relegated Sheffield Wednesday.

Their recent run of form has also seen them keep three clean sheets in four matches across all competitions in November, playing a major role in helping them maintain the best defensive record in League One, with no side having conceded fewer than their 13 goals.

Saturday will mark their 15th league outing of the campaign, a fixture that they marked with a 1-0 victory over Peterborough United just over a year ago to move top of the table, highlighting the stark contrast with their performances at the same stage last season.

As for Blackpool, they look set to play their third match under interim manager Thompson, who took charge at Bloomfield Road following the departure of Ian Evatt, who was relieved of his duties after a 57-game spell with the Seasiders.

Evatt left the Lancashire-based club following a 1-0 defeat to AFC Wimbledon, a result that left Blackpool 20th and level on points with teams in the relegation zone.

Thompson, who has previously had three other spells as Blackpool's caretaker manager, oversaw a 2-1 defeat to fellow strugglers Wigan Athletic before guiding his side to a 1-1 draw with recently relegated Leicester City.

The stalemate with the Foxes came courtesy of an 84th-minute equaliser from Ennis in a match where the Seasiders had just 22.9% possession and faced 30 shots, but the unlikely point was enough to keep them outside the relegation zone.

Thompson is expected to remain in charge for this weekend's fixture, with Blackpool yet to appoint a permanent successor to Evatt, while Matt Bloomfield and Richie Wellens have both been linked with the vacancy.

Should Blackpool secure what would be just their fourth league win of the season this weekend, they could head into December with a three-point cushion above the drop zone, giving their next permanent manager an opportunity to take charge of a side unbeaten in two matches, although they face a Stevenage team that defeated them both home and away last season.

Stevenage form (all competitions):.

Blackpool form (all competitions):.

After drawing at home to Sheffield Wednesday in midweek, Revell will be keen to keep his side unchanged and has the luxury of doing so after his squad came through the match without any fresh injury concerns.

Tommy Setford has played a key role in Stevenage's impressive defensive record, and the 20-year-old goalkeeper is expected to retain his place as he bids to register his fifth clean sheet of the season.

Revell will, however, remain without Jasper Pattenden, Dan Kemp and Jordan Roberts, who are all still sidelined through injury.

For what is likely to be Thompson's third and final match in charge of Blackpool, the former midfielder will once again be without several first-team players.

A sickness bug kept Bailey Peacock-Farrell, Josh Bowler and Finley Munroe out of recent matches, but all three returned for the clash with the Foxes and are expected to feature again this weekend.

Dale Taylor, defenders Josh Earl, Fraser Horsfall and Michael Ihiekwe, as well as captain George Honeyman, are all likely to remain unavailable for the trip to Hertfordshire.

Having scored his second goal of the season after coming off the bench last time out, Ennis is likely to be rewarded with a starting place and could replace either Dion Charles or Jerry Yates.

Stevenage possible starting lineup:.

Setford; Vancooten, Casey, Piergianni, Earley; Phillips, Thompson; Sanderson, Broggio, Patterson; Magennis.

Blackpool possible starting lineup:.

Peacock-Farrell; Lyons, Casey, Ashworth, Munroe; Niskanen, Brown, Morgan, Hamilton; Ennis, Charles.

With one of the best defensive sides in the English Football League meeting a team who have struggled to score on a regular basis, we expect Boro to edge a low-scoring contest.

We expect the Seasiders' struggles to continue with Boro making it four unbeaten in the league and closing out November with a sixth win of the season.

  • The struggling League One side are looking for a newly introduced manager after firing Ian Evatt on his birthday last week.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 09:12 EST, 25 November 2026 | Updated: 09:12 EST, 25 November 2026.

Conor Coady has emerged as one of the candidates to become latest head coach at Blackpool.

The struggling League One side are looking for a newly introduced manager after firing Ian Evatt on his birthday last week.

They salvaged a draw against Leicester City on Tuesday to stay just above the drop zone in 20th place with caretaker Steve Thompson in charge.

The Tangerines are understood to have been inundated with applications with the likes of Conor Hourihane, who left Leicester City as assistant manager earlier this month, Matt Bloomfield, formerly Oxford United boss, and Richie Wellens of Leyton Orient among the leading names in the frame.

However, Daily Mail Sport understands former England, Wolves and Everton defender Coady is also being considered.

Conor Coady, pictured here working as England Under-21s assistant, could take over at Blackpool.

The 33-year-old retired from playing on November 6 after stints with Wrexham and Charlton Athletic and took up a role as assistant to Lee Carsley in the England U21 set-up in September, replacing Ashley Cole.

Coady had also been helping out within his first club Liverpool's U21 set-up, prior to his deadline day departure from Wrexham.

He is keen to make the step up in club coaching and was linked with a role at Barnsley in recent weeks.
